Season one half with salt and garlic powder to taste.For sweet wraps, add half of a banana to the other half of the batter and blend until smooth.
Reserve the remaining banana for the filling.
Lightly oil a non-stick skillet and heat it over medium heat.
Pour enough batter into the skillet to make one wrap, then use the back of a spoon to spread it into a thin, even circle.
Cook until the underside is golden brown and the surface looks set.
Carefully flip the wrap and cook the other side until lightly browned.
Repeat with the remaining batter, adding a little more oil to the skillet when necessary.
Serve the savory wraps with your favorite fillings, e.g. avocado or hummus.
For a simple sweet version, spread vegan chocolate cream over a wrap, top it with slices of the remaining banana, and fold it into a triangle.

items.title: Homemade Vegan Liverwurst
items.creator: Elavegan
ingredients: 3/4 cup firm silken tofu (or regular tofu)
steps: You can watch the video for visual instructions.Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Meanwhile, finely dice the onion and chop the garlic.
Sauté the onion for 5 minutes until softened and lightly golden.
Add the garlic in the final 30 seconds.
Drain, rinse, and pat the kidney beans dry, then add them to a food processor along with the tofu.
Add the tomato paste, tamari, liquid smoke, sautéed aromatics, and all the spices.
Pulse to your desired texture (I like mine creamy but still slightly chunky), scraping down the sides as needed.
Taste and adjust any seasonings, including the salt, pepper, and liquid smoke.
Transfer the vegan liverwurst spread to a jar and refrigerate for at least 1 hour to firm up.
Enjoy on gluten-free bread!

items.title: Italian Abbracci Cookies (chocolate and cream)
items.creator: Inside the Rustic Kitchen
ingredients: 185 g (13 tablespoons) unsalted butter ((at room temperature))
130 g (2/3 cup) caster sugar (superfine) (or use granulated)
210 g (1 1/2 cups) Italian 00 flour ( (or all-purpose flour))
180 g (1 1/4 cup plus 1 teaspoon) Italian 00 flour ( (or all-purpose flour))
steps: First, put the butter and sugar in the bowl of a stand mixer with a paddle attachment and beat them together until light and fluffy (about 5 minutes).
Whisk the whole egg and 2 egg yolks together in a small bowl, then with the mixer running slowly, pour the eggs in one third at a time, letting the mixture absorb the egg before adding more.
Once the egg is fully incorporated, add the baking powder, vanilla, honey and a pinch of salt.
Mix until just combined.
Put a large mixing bowl on your kitchen scale and weigh the whole mixture.
Use a spatula to scrape out as much as possible.
Once you know the weight of the whole mixture, divide the mixture in half into two separate mixing bowls.
Add the 30g cocoa powder and 180g flour to one mixing bowl and 1 tablespoon of heavy cream and 210g flour to the other mixing bowl.
Working with one batch of dough at a time, use a fork to mix the dough until large crumbs form.
Then use your hands to bring the dough together and shape it into a large disc.
Wrap the dough in plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Once the cookie dough is chilled and firm, remove it from the fridge.
Cut a small piece of cocoa dough and weigh out 10g, then roll it into a small ball.
Do the same with the panna dough, so you have one 10g ball of each.
Next, roll each ball into a small log around 2.5 inches (6cm) in length.
Shape each one into a ‘C’ shape, then gently place the panna dough over the cocoa dough at the ends and press down to join them together to create the classic abbracci shape.
Arrange the cookies on a lined baking tray about 1/2 inch apart, then refrigerate them for 20 minutes.
I usually do this in batches to save space.
Preheat the oven to 170℃/340℉ conventional (static).
Once chilled, bake the cookies for 19 minutes.
Let them cool in the tray, then move to a cooling rack.
Store in an airtight container.

items.title: Zucchini Puffer | mit Feta | Felicitas Then
items.creator: Felicitas Then
steps: ⁠ ⁠Die Zucchini waschen, die Enden abschneiden und grob raspeln.
Anschließend salzen und einige Minuten ziehen lassen.
Das Salz entzieht der Zucchini Wasser und sorgt später für besonders knusprige Puffer.
⁠ ⁠Die geraspelte Zucchini auf ein sauberes Geschirrtuch geben und sehr gründlich ausdrücken. Je trockener die Zucchini ist, desto knuspriger werden die Puffer.
⁠ ⁠Schalotte fein hacken oder ebenfalls raspeln. Nach Wunsch etwas Knoblauch und Zitronenabrieb dazugeben.
⁠ ⁠Dill oder Minze fein hacken und unter die Zucchini mischen. Minze gibt den Puffern eine besonders frische, griechische Note.
⁠ ⁠Ei, Mehl, Pfeffer und etwas Chili hinzufügen. Zusätzliches Salz ist meist nicht nötig, da die Zucchini bereits gesalzen wurde.
⁠ ⁠Feta zerbröseln und unter die Masse heben. Alternativ funktioniert auch Parmesan.
⁠ ⁠Olivenöl in einer Pfanne erhitzen.
Mit einem Löffel kleine Portionen der Masse hineingeben und flach drücken.
Die Puffer bei mittlerer bis etwas höherer Hitze braten und erst wenden, wenn die Unterseite schön gebräunt und stabil ist.
⁠ ⁠Von beiden Seiten goldbraun und knusprig braten und direkt servieren.

items.title: Schwangerschafts-Cravings 🩵 Part 1 - Lasagne
items.creator: Sallys Welt
steps: evtl. Paprikamark
ca. 12–15 Lasagneblätter
Und jetzt wird geschichtet, gebacken und anschließend ordentlich geschlemmt. 😋❤️

items.title: Italian Roasted Marinated Peppers
items.creator: Inside the Rustic Kitchen
ingredients: 2 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil (plus extra for roasting)
steps: Preheat the oven to 200℃/400℉ fan or 220℃/425℉ conventional.
Lightly drizzle the peppers in olive oil and place them on a baking tray.
Roast them in the oven for 30-35 minutes, until soft and charred.
Place the peppers in a large bowl and cover it with plastic wrap (cling film).
Let the peppers cool for at least 30 minutes, but you can also wait until they are completely cold.
Once cooled, remove the seeds and stalks from the peppers and peel off the skin.
This should come away very easily.
Cut the peppers into strips and arrange them on a serving plate or dish and season them with a pinch of salt.
Finely slice the garlic and add it on top of the peppers, then scatter over some torn basil leaves.
Combine the olive oil and balsamic vinegar with a good pinch of salt and pepper, then whisk it together until combined.
Pour the dressing over the peppers, then cover with plastic wrap or foil and leave to marinate for at least 30 minutes before serving.
Tip: The peppers taste best once they have been left to marinate for a few hours.

items.title: DIDDL is BACK!
items.creator: Sallys Welt
ingredients: je 2 g Lebensmittelfarbpaste in Gelb Blau und Pink
Kuchen zuerst 15 Minuten bei 160 °C Ober-/Unterhitze backen
steps: Dann eine hitzebeständige Schale mit Wasser in den Ofen stellen - der Wasserdampf sorgt dafür, dass der Käsekuchen schön saftig und cremig bleibt
Temperatur anschließend auf 130 °C Ober-/Unterhitze reduzieren und den Kuchen weitere 45–60 Minuten backen.
Danach aus dem Ofen nehmen, abkühlen lassen und mindestens 2 Stunden kalt stellen

items.title: Der perfekte Flammkuchen: hauchdünn & richtig knusprig
items.creator: Thomas kocht
steps: Backzeit: ca. 7 Minuten
Probiert den Flammkuchen unbedingt aus und schreibt mir in die Kommentare, wie er euch gelungen ist!
Mein Name ist Thomas und ich bin gelernter Koch seit jetzt schon 20 Jahren.
Neben dem Kochen ist das Backen eine weitere Leidenschaft von mir.

items.title: Roasted Cherry Tomato and Ricotta Pasta
items.creator: Inside the Rustic Kitchen
ingredients: 1/3 cup (20g) Parmigiano Reggiano ((finely grated) plus extra for serving)
steps: Preheat the oven to 180℃/350℉fan or 200℃/400℉ static.
Cut the cherry tomatoes in half and place them on a baking tray.
Add the 3 cloves of garlic (keep the skins on) then drizzle over 2-3 tablespoons of olive oil.
Arrange the tomatoes so they are facing cut side up.
Sprinkle over the chilli flakes and a good pinch of salt and pepper then roast in the oven for around 25 minutes until soft, jammy and slightly charred.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil and salt it well.
Once roasted, transfer the cherry tomatoes to a blender.
Remove the skins from the garlic and add that to the blender too alongside the ricotta and grated Parmigiano Reggiano.
Blitz until smooth.
Taste for seasoning and add more salt if needed.
Transfer the sauce to a pan and add a small handful of torn basil leaves.
Add your pasta to the water and cook until al dente.
As the pasta is cooking, heat the sauce on low.
Add 1/4 cup (60ml) of pasta water to loosen the sauce and stir until combined.
Add more pasta water as needed.
I usually add 1/2 cup (120ml) total before adding the pasta then a splash more once the pasta has been added.
Transfer the cooked pasta to the sauce and toss until coated.
Add more pasta water as needed until you have a smooth and emulsified sauce.
Serve in bowls topped with more Parmigiano.

items.title: Pesto selber machen
items.creator: Thomas kocht
steps: Wichtig: das Wasser und die Eiswürfel werden wieder ausgegossen und kommen nicht in die Pesto. Das ist nur zum Kühlen des Gefäßes.
Traditionell werden die Pinienkerne für Pesto Genovese nicht geröstet. Wer sie trotzdem rösten möchte: unbedingt vollständig abkühlen lassen, bevor sie ins Pesto kommen.
💚 Für eine schöne grüne Farbe das Pesto möglichst schnell und kühl verarbeiten – langes Mixen und Wärme lassen es schneller dunkel werden.
Pesto im Kühlschrank lagern und die Oberfläche immer mit einer dünnen Schicht Olivenöl bedecken, damit möglichst wenig Sauerstoff herankommt.
Licht lässt die schöne grüne Farbe ebenfalls schneller verschwinden – deshalb dunkel lagern oder das Glas z.
B. mit Alufolie umwickeln.
Am besten innerhalb von 3-5 Tagen verbrauchen. Für längere Lagerung lässt sich Pesto sehr gut einfrieren.

items.title: Sushi selber machen - Reis perfekt kochen
items.creator: Thomas kocht
steps: Alles vorsichtig erwärmen, bis sich Zucker und Salz gelöst haben – kochen muss die Mischung nicht. Anschließend nach Geschmack unter den noch warmen Sushi-Reis arbeiten.
Beim Fisch gilt: Wenn ihr ihn roh für Sushi oder Sashimi verwenden möchtet, fragt beim Händler gezielt nach Fisch, der für den Rohverzehr geeignet ist.
Und falls die ersten Rollen noch nicht perfekt aussehen: Das ist völlig normal. Sushi rollen ist vor allem Übungssache – mit jeder Rolle wird es einfacher.
Viel Spaß beim Nachmachen!
Mein Name ist Thomas und ich bin gelernter Koch seit jetzt schon 20 Jahren.

items.title: Caffè Shakerato (Italian Iced Coffee)
items.creator: Inside the Rustic Kitchen
ingredients: 1 double espresso or strong coffee ((60ml or 1/4 cup) I use Lavazza espresso ground coffee)
steps: Brew your double espresso using your coffee machine.
Stir in the sugar and let it dissolve for a few seconds.
Fill your cocktail shaker with ice and pour over the sweetened espresso.
Give it a good shake for about 30 seconds (as if you're shaking a cocktail) and strain it into your serving glass.

items.title: Ofen-Aubergine mit Salat: leicht gemachter Hingucker
items.creator: Tom Pingel
steps: Backofen auf 200 Grad (180 Grad Umluft) vorheizen.
Auberginen halbieren.
Die Hälften der Länge nach fächerförmig einschneiden, sodass sie am Stielende noch 1 cm dick zusammenhängen.
Auberginen andrücken, damit ein Fächer entsteht, leicht salzen, mit 2 El Olivenöl beträufeln und auf ein mit Backpapier belegtes Backblech legen.
Im heißen Backofen auf der 2.
Schiene von unten 30 Minuten garen.
Inzwischen Tomaten in Scheiben schneiden und mit Salz und Pfeffer würzen.
Mozzarella abtropfen lassen und in Scheiben schneiden.
Für das Dressing Zitronensaft mit 2 El Öl, 2 El Wasser, Honig, Salz und Pfeffer verrühren.
Rucola waschen, verlesen und mit dem Dressing mischen.
Basilikumblätter abzupfen.
Auberginen aus dem Backofen nehmen.
Mozzarella und Tomatenscheiben abwechselnd zwischen den Auberginen verteilen.
Mit dem Rucolasalat und Basilikum servieren.

items.title: Knusprige Dinkelbrötchen mit Hafer: mit Übernachtgare
items.creator: Malte's Kitchen
ingredients: 125 g Zarte Haferflocken (+ mehr für Deko)
steps: Beide Dinkelmehlsorten in einer Schüssel mit den Haferflocken mischen.
300 g Wasser zugeben und mit einer Gabel grob verrühren.
Es bleiben Mehlnester stehen, dass ist nicht schlimm!Den Vorteig 30 Minuten abgedeckt ruhen lassen, damit nichts austrocknet.
Die Hefe und den Zucker in den restlichen 50 g Wasser unter Rühren auflösen.
Die Hefe zum Vorteig geben.
Salz und Quark zufügen und mit dem Knethaken in der Küchenmaschine 8 Minuten kneten.Einmal den Rand mit einem Silikonspatel reinigen und die Reste zum Teig geben.
Den fertig gekneteten Teig in der Schüssel lassen und diese abdecken (oder in einen passenden Behälter mit Deckel geben) und über Nacht (10-12 Stunden) im Kühlschrank gehen lassen.
Das Teigvolumen wird sich verdoppeln oder gar verdreifachen!
Am nächsten Tag ein Backblech mit Backpapier auslegen.
2 EL Haferflocken auf einen flachen Teller geben.Die Arbeitsfläche leicht mehlen und den Teig mit einer Teigkarte aus der Schüssel darauf schaben.
Den Teig in acht gleich große Teile teilen (bei mir ca.
150 g je Brötchen).Jedes Teigstück dehnen und falten und anschließend zu einem runden Brötchen schleifen.
Das Teigstück mit Wasser leicht befeuchten und in die Haferflocken auf dem Teller drücken.
Auf das Backpapier setzen und genügend Abstand lassen.
Liegen die Brötchen zu eng beieinander, werden sie nicht so knusprig.
Das Backblech auf unterste (!) Schiene in den kalten (!) Backofen schieben und eine Temperatur von 230 Grad Ober-/Unterhitze einstellen.
Die Dinkelbrötchen für 26 Minuten backen, bis sie eine schöne Farbe haben.

items.title: Torta Nua (Italian Cake with Pastry Cream)
items.creator: Inside the Rustic Kitchen
ingredients: 3 large egg yolks ((I use golden yolks but this is not necessary))
280 g (2 cups) Italian 00 flour ((can also use all-purpose flour))
180 g (3/4 cup plus 2 tablespoons) caster/superfine sugar ((can also use granulated))
steps: Peel the lemon in strips using a vegetable peeler and place it in a large saucepan with the milk and vanilla extract.
Heat the milk until it just starts to simmer then turn off the heat immediately (photo 1).
Meanwhile, in a large bowl, combine the egg yolks, sugar and cornstarch and whisk until smooth and combined (photo 2).
Add a splash of the hot milk to the egg mixture and whisk it in.
Place a sieve over the bowl and pour in the remaining milk, straining out the lemon peel.
Give it a good whisk to avoid the eggs overcooking (photos 3 and 4).
Pour the mixture back into the large saucepan you heated the milk in and heat on a medium-low heat until very thick.
I use a wooden spoon until I can feel the pastry cream starting to thicken, then switch to a hand whisk to avoid any lumps.
Pour the pastry cream into a clean bowl and cover it with plastic wrap, directly on top of the cream to stop a skin from forming.
Let it cool for 20-30 minutes (photos 5 and 6).
Preheat the oven to 180C (350F) static (non-fan oven).
Grease your cake pan with butter and line the bottom with parchment paper.
Place the cake pan on a baking tray and set aside (photo 7).
Melt the butter in a saucepan and let it cool (warm is fine, just not hot).
Warm the milk in a separate saucepan so it’s not fridge cold; it should be tepid and not hot.
Add the flour and baking powder to a bowl and give it a quick whisk to aerate it (photo 8).
Put the eggs, sugar and lemon zest to a the bowl of a stand mixer (or use a large mixing bowl and an electric hand whisk).
Beat with the whisk attachment on medium speed.
Once the mixture combines, continue to beat it for 2 minutes; it should be frothy (photos 9 and 10).
Next, add the melted butter and whisk it in, followed by the milk.
While whisking, add the flour and baking powder a spoonful at a time until it is all used up.
Whisk for a few seconds until thoroughly combined (make sure to scrape down the sides of any excess flour and whisk it in) (photo 11).
Pour the batter into your prepared cake pan, then dollop over spoonfuls of pastry cream.
I use roughly 2 tablespoons of pastry cream per dollop and place them in a circle around the outside, then in the middle (photos 12 and 13).
Bake in the oven for 35 minutes (check with a skewer inserted into the sponge).
Remove from the oven and let it sit for 10 minutes before removing the springform ring (if using) (photo 14).
Once completely cool and just before serving, dust some powdered sugar over the top, cut into slices and serve.

items.title: Polpette di ceci fritte
items.creator: Giuseppe Coppola
steps: Schiacciare con la forchetta i ceci con il succo del limone, sale e pepe.
Trasferire il tutto nel vaso del minipimer, unire 5 cucchiai d’olio extravergine e azionare brevemente l’apparecchio per ottenere una salsa omogenea.
Trasferirla in una ciotola e incorporare l’uovo, il timo e la farina amalgamando bene.
Scaldare l’olio di semi in una padella e friggete le polpettine prelevando il composto con un cucchiaino.
Farle dorare da ambo i lati, scolare l’unto in eccesso con carta assorbente e servirle calde.

items.title: Blumenkohlsteak mit kernigem Crunch: so schmeckt Blumenkohl jedem
items.creator: Lisa Niemann
steps: Blumenkohl putzen, äußere Blätter entfernen, den Strunk knapp abschneiden.
Den mittleren Teil des Blumenkohls in 2 cm dicke Scheiben schneiden.
Darauf achten, dass die Schnitte durch den Strunk gehen, damit die Steaks zusammenhalten.
Die Scheiben und den restlichen Blumenkohl (die äußeren, losen Teile) In einem breiten Topf mit reichlich kochendem Salzwasser 3–4 Minuten vorgaren.
Mit einer Schaumkelle vorsichtig herausnehmen, eiskalt abschrecken, auf Küchenpapier abtropfen lassen.
Backofen auf 200 Grad (Umluft 180 Grad) vorheizen.
Zitronenschale fein abreiben, den Saft auspressen.
Thymianblättchen abzupfen.
Zitronenschale, Zitronensaft, Thymian, Paprikapulver, Currypaste, 1 Tl Honig und 4 El Olivenöl in einer Schüssel verrühren, mit Salz und Pfeffer würzen.
Beide Seiten der Blumenkohlsteaks mit der Marinade bestreichen, auf ein mit Backpapier belegtes Backblech legen und im heißen Ofen 15–20 Minuten backen.
Cashewkerne, Haferflocken und Sonnenblumenkerne in einer Pfanne ohne Fett rösten.
Joghurt glattrühren.
Salat waschen, verlesen und trocknen.
2 El Öl mit Balsamico, 1 Tl Honig, Salz und Pfeffer zu einem Dressing verrühren.
Blumenkohlsteaks mit Joghurt und der Nussmischung toppen, auf Salat anrichten und servieren.

items.title: No Knead Lievito Madre Bread
items.creator: An Italian in my Kitchen
ingredients: 110 g active lievito madre (broken in pieces)
steps: In a small bowl add 122 ml of the water and the lievito madre, mix together (it's easiest to mix with clean hands) add the honey and mix together.

In a large bowl whisk together the flours and salt, add the lievito madre mixture and remaining water, mix together with a wooden spoon or spatula, cover with plastic wrap or a clean tea towel and place in a warm draft free area for approximately 10-16 hours or until doubled.
Move the dough to a semolina floured flat surface and fold to form a loaf, dust lightly with semolina flour then cover with a tea towel and let rise 2-3 hours in a warm draft free area.
Place a parchment paper lined dutch oven (with the lid on) in the oven, then pre-heat oven to 400F/200C.
Let the oven heat for about 20 minutes.
Carefully remove the hot dutch oven from the oven, remove the lid and flip the dough (seam side up) into the dutch oven.
Cover and bake for 30 minutes, remove the lid and continue to bake for approximately 10-15 minutes.
Move the dough (with the parchment paper) immediately to a wire rack to cool completely before slicing.
Dough is baked when the internal temperature is 190-210F / 88-99C.

items.title: Saftiger Mohnkuchen mit Streuseln: Klassiker wie von Oma
items.creator: Rike Dittloff
steps: Ei trennen, Eiweiß für die Füllung aufheben.
Für den Teig Mehl, Zucker, Zitronenabrieb und Eigelb in eine Schüssel geben.
Mit den Quirlen des Handrührers vermengen.
Dabei die geschmolzene Butter nach und nach zugeben.
Die Hälfte des Kuchenteigs in die gefettete Backform geben und mit den Fingern zum Kuchenboden festdrücken.
Kuchenboden und restlichen Teig in den Kühlschrank stellen.
Inzwischen Puddingpulver mit etwa 100 ml der kalten Milch glatt rühren.
Übrige Milch aufkochen, vom Herd nehmen, angerührtes Pulver und Zucker mit einem Schneebesen einrühren.
Mohn einrieseln lassen und gründlich unterrühren.
Mohn-Pudding-Mischung etwa eine Minute unter Rühren kochen lassen.
Mohnmischung vom Herd nehmen und 5 Minuten quellen lassen.
Danach in eine Schüssel füllen und etwa 10 Minuten abkühlen lassen.
Eiweiß mit den Quirlen des Handrührers zum festen Eischnee schlagen.
Vorsichtig nach und nach unter den abgekühlten Mohn-Pudding heben.
Mohn-Pudding auf den Teigboden in die Form geben und gleichmäßig verstreichen.
Restlichen Teig als Streusel auf dem Kuchen verteilen.
Mohnkuchen im heißen Backofen bei 175 Grad Umluft auf der 2.
Schiene von unten etwa 60 Minuten backen.

items.title: Omas cremige Milchnudeln
items.creator: Malte's Kitchen
steps: Die Milch zusammen mit dem Vanillezucker, der Butter und der Prise Salz in einen Topf geben und heiß werden lassen.
Die Nudeln zufügen und unter häufigem Rühren leicht köcheln lassen, bis die Nudeln weich geworden sind.
Das dauert bei Hörnchennudeln ca.
12 Minuten.
Die Sahne und das Puddingpulver zufügen und noch 2 Minuten unterrühren, bis die Milchnudeln schön cremig geworden sind.
Servieren und die Milchnudeln nach Geschmack mit Zimt und Zucker bestreuen.
Ich esse sie auch gerne mit Pflaumen- oder Apfelkompott und bestreue sie mit ein paar angerösteten Mandelblättchen.

items.title: Chocolate Zucchini Cake Recipe
items.creator: An Italian in my Kitchen
ingredients: ¾ cup + 1 tablespoon cocoa powder (unsweetened) ((30 grams))
⅓-⅔ cup nuts finely chopped (walnuts, pecans or hazelnuts)
¾ cup + 1 tablespoon butter (melted and cooled) ((200 grams))
¼-⅓ cup chocolate chips (small or regular, semi sweet or milk)
steps: Pre-heat oven to 350F (180C).
Grease and flour an 8 or 9 inch (20-23cm) cake pan.
In a medium bowl whisk together the flour, cocoa, salt, baking powder and nuts.
Set aside.

In the mixing bowl beat together the sugar, eggs & yolk until light, about 3 minutes on medium/low speed, then beat in the melted cooled butter and then the grated zucchini add the dry ingredients and combine until smooth, about 1 minute.

Pour into the prepared cake pan, sprinkle with some chocolate chips if desired and bake for about 50-60 minutes test for doneness with a tooth pick (it may take more or less time depending on your oven).
Let cool before serving.

items.title: Easy Italian Butterfly Salad
items.creator: An Italian in my Kitchen
ingredients: 3 cups pasta (cooked) ((small past / I used bow tie pasta))
20-25 grape or cherry tomatoes ((cut in half))
steps: In a large pot of boiling salted water cook the pasta al dente.
Drain and rinse in cold water. (Only rinse pasta in cold water if making a cold pasta salad)
In a small bowl combine the olive oil, balsamic, oregano, salt, basil and dash of pepper.
Stir or whisk to combine.
In a large bowl add the tuna, corn, mozzarella balls, tomatoes and fresh chopped basil, then add the cooked drained pasta and mix, then drizzle the dressing on top and gently combine.
Can be served immediately or cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate approximately 1 hour before serving.

items.title: Easy Lemon Charlotte / Icebox Cake
items.creator: An Italian in my Kitchen
ingredients: 1½ cups cream whole, heavy or whipping cream (cold) at least 30% fat content
steps: In a small pot heat the water, peel and sugar, heat on medium heat until sugar has dissolved, then simmer on low medium heat for approximately 3 - 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and let cool, then stir in the juice or limoncello.
In a large bowl beat the mascarpone, icing sugar (sifted), zest and cream, until very thick.
Cut some of the lady fingers to fit the height of a 7½ - 8 inch springform pan.
Place the cut fingers touching around the pan, place lady fingers cut and or whole to fit the bottom of the pan as a base. (Remaining lady fingers are for the 2nd layer).
Brush a little of the syrup lightly (very lightly) over the lady fingers that are around the pan, then spoon half of the syrup on the cut lady finger base.

Spread half the filling over the base then top with another layer of lady fingers drizzle the remaining syrup on top, then spread the remaining filling on top of the 2nd layer of lady fingers (or use a pastry tip and decorate the top with the filling).
Cover with plastic and refrigerate for at least 3 - 4 hours or better over night.
Remove the pan before serving.

items.title: Grilled Pork Chops
items.creator: An Italian in my Kitchen
steps: In a food processor or blender combine the garlic, basil, lemon juice, olive oil, salt and pepper, blend until smooth.
Spread on both sides of the chops and let stand for 20-30 minutes.
Grill the chops for approximately 6-8 minutes on each side, turning once.
Internal temperature for pork is 145F/63C.
Serve immediately.

items.title: Italian Cream and Fresh Fruit Tart
items.creator: An Italian in my Kitchen
ingredients: ¼ cup butter ((if needed add an extra 1 or 2 tablespoons))
steps: In a 7 - 8 inch / 18-20 cm round spring form pan melt butter over low heat add graham cracker crumbs, combine and press down firmly, refrigerate for approximately 20-30 minutes.
Heat milk and cream until hot but do not boil, let cool to warm.

In a medium pot add egg yolks and sugar, whisk to combine, whisk in flour and vanilla, place pot over low heat add warm milk/cream mixture and continue whisking (do not stop stirring) until very thick, remove from pot and place in a glass bowl, cover with plastic wrap, make sure plastic is touching cream mixture, let cool 15 minutes then place in refrigerator until very cold, approximately 3 hours.
In a medium bowl mix together sliced fruit and sugar.
Let stand 10-15 minutes mix to combine.
Remove base from fridge, cover with filling, spread evenly, then top with fresh fruit.
Refrigerate an hour or even over night.
Remove sides of spring form pan, slice and serve.

items.title: Eggplant Pie
items.creator: Real Greek Recipes
ingredients: 300 grams (10 ounces) sweet red peppers (finely diced)
80 grams (⅓ cup) crushed tomatoes (canned) (or fresh, ripe, grated tomatoes)
70 grams (½ cup) grated Kefalotyri cheese (see text above for substitutions )
300 grams (2½ cups) all-purpose flour (+ extra for rolling the filo)
1 tablespoon red wine vinegar (other types work too)
160 ml (⅔ cup) water (might need slightly more or less)
100 ml olive oil (for brushing the filo)
1-2 tablespoons sesame seeds (to sprinkle on top of the pie)
steps: Prepare the eggplant.
Cut off the tops and bottoms.
Then dice into small pieces.
Soak in plenty of water for at least 30 minutes.
Then drain in a strainer.
Make the filo dough.
In a bowl, whisk together the flour, salt, and baking powder.
Pour in the olive oil, then slowly add the water while kneading the dough.
It should feel sticky but without leaving fragments on your hands.
Rest the dough.
Shape the dough into a ball.
Dust the top and bottom with flour.
Cover the bowl with a dampened tea towel or plastic wrap and rest at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Heat a generous amount of olive oil in a medium-sized cooking pot or large saute pan.
Saute the onions then add the eggplant in batches.
Season with salt.
Cook until soft and mellow.
The more you cook the eggplant at this point the stronger its flavor will be inside the filling.
Add the red peppers and cook for a minute.
Stir in the tomato paste and crushed tomatoes.
Cook until the filling drains to the point where it starts to get sticky at the bottom.
Take the pot off the heat.
Add the dried oregano, paprika, and basil.
Stir and set aside to cool.
Preheat the oven to 180°C / 350°F.
Shape the filo dough into a log and cut it into 6 pieces.
Each piece is a filo.
2 for the bottom, one between the filling layers, and 3 for the top of the pie.
Shape each piece into a round ball and keep aside, covered.
Make the first filo.
Dust the work surface with flour and place the dough ball.
Dust the dough ball with flour also.
Start rolling in all directions with a rolling pin until you have a round filo big enough to cover the bottom and sides of the pan.
Always dust the bottom and top of the filo with flour as you roll, so it won't stick.
Also, flip the filo as seen in the video below.
Brush a 31 cm (12-inch) round pan with olive oil.
Roll the filo around the rolling pin and then unroll it inside the pan.
Gently pull it a bit to cover the sides.
Brush with olive oil.
Make the second filo.

items.title: Eggplant Saganaki
items.creator: Real Greek Recipes
ingredients: 150 grams (5.3 ounces) feta cheese (crumbled into large chunks )
50 grams (7 tablespoons) grated Kefalotyri cheese (see the text above for substitution)
500 ml (2 cups) hot water or vegetable stock
steps: Heat a splash of olive oil in a cooking pot over moderate heat.
Saute the onion and garlic until golden.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes, the hot water or stock, the bay leaf, smoked paprika, and season with salt and pepper.
Simmer the sauce partly covered over moderate heat until thickened.
Meanwhile, prepare the eggplant.
Slice off the tops and bottoms of the eggplant.
Cut it in half and then into 2½-3 cm (1-1¼ inch) thick slices.
Generously coat the bottom of a frying pan with olive oil.
Heat over high heat.
Pan-fry the eggplant slices until deep golden, lightly browned on each side.
Only the outer part should soften because the eggplant will cook in the sauce as well.
NOTE: Pan-fry in batches, adding more oil before cooking the next batch as necessary.
Eggplant soaks oil like a sponge.
Add the pan-fried eggplant to the cooking pot with the thickened sauce.
Cook covered, over moderate heat for about 20 minutes until the eggplant softens.
If necessary, add a splash of water.
Stir in the dried oregano, parsley, feta, and Kefalotyri cheese.
Turn off the heat and leave the pot on the hot stove for a minute or two until both cheeses soften and melt.
Serve warm with plenty of crusty bread for dipping.

items.title: Mung Bean Soup
items.creator: Real Greek Recipes
ingredients: 200 grams (1 cup) dry mung beans ((whole green not split))
1 branch of celery (including the leaves) (finely chopped)
60 ml (¼ cup) extra virgin olive oil (+ extra to drizzle on top)
750 ml (3 cups) hot water or vegetable stock
steps: Soak mung beans for 2-3 hours in plenty of cold water.
Bring to a boil for 2 minutes, then drain.
Add the mung beans, onion, garlic, tomato, carrot, zucchini, celery, and 750 ml water or stock to a cooking pot and bring to a simmer.
Season with salt and pepper.
Cook over medium-low heat for about an hour, or until the mung beans are tender.
Stir in the olive oil, lemon juice, and oregano.
Simmer for 10 minutes longer, stirring occasionally, until thick and creamy.
If necessary, raise the heat slightly to help the soup thicken.
Serve drizzled with raw extra-virgin olive oil, and season with freshly ground pepper on top.

items.title: Easy Greek Yogurt Torte (no-bake)
items.creator: Real Greek Recipes
ingredients: 400 grams (14 ounces) petit beurres (digestive cookies or graham crackers)
steps: Whisk yogurt, condensed milk, and vanilla extract until fluffy and creamy.
Whisk vigorously for 5 minutes.
Break the biscuits into chunky pieces and stir into the mixture in batches.
Stir until fully combined.
Transfer mixture to a 26 cm (10-inch) Springform cake pan or cake dish of similar size.
Smooth with a spoon on top.
Refrigerate for 6-8 hours or longer for a more uniform, mousse-like texture.
Or freeze for 3-4 hours and serve as a semi-fredo torte.
Top with your favorite jam and/or fruit and nuts.
Cut into 12 large pieces, serve and enjoy!

items.title: Baked Stuffed Eggplant with Rice
items.creator: Real Greek Recipes
ingredients: 550 grams (1.2 pounds) potatoes (peeled and cut into wedges)
100 grams (1 small) sweet red pepper (finely chopped)
170 grams (14 tablespoons) round grain white rice (such as Karolina or Arborio)
140 ml (⅓ + ¼ cups) extra virgin olive oil (+ extra splash for sauteing)
steps: Preheat oven to 200°C / 400°F.
Slice the top and bottom of each eggplant.
Then slice one side lengthwise to create a lid.
Scoop the eggplant flesh by running a sharp knife around the inside of the eggplant, then use a spoon to scoop most of the flesh, leaving a 1 cm-thick wall.
Don't discard the flesh.
Chop the flesh to use it in the filling.You can soak the eggplant in water to avoid oxidation and browning until you have prepared them all.
Coat the bottom of a frying pan with olive oil.
Heat over moderate heat.
Saute the onion and garlic until soft and translucent.
Add the chopped eggplant flesh.
Season with salt and pepper.
Raise the heat to high and cook until it softens.
Add the tomato paste and cook for a minute, stirring often.
Add the chopped/diced tomatoes and red pepper.
Cook until they soften as well.
Take off the heat.
Stir in the rice, parsley, basil, 1 teaspoon dried oregano, pine nuts, and ⅓ cup (80 ml) olive oil.
Stuff each eggplant and put its lid on.
Place in a pan that fits them with the potato wedges all around them.
Toss the chopped tomato on top of the potatoes.
Drizzle with ¼ cup (60 ml) olive oil, and sprinkle the remaining 1 teaspoon of dried oregano all over.
Season everything with salt and pepper and pour 310 ml (1 + ¼ cups) water from the side.
Cover with parchment paper and secure with aluminum foil on top.
Bake for 1 hour and 20 minutes.
Uncover and roast for a few minutes more for the potatoes and eggplants to get some color.
If there's too much water in the pan, you can raise the heat to 220°C / 430°F for the final roast.
Rest inside the oven for 30 minutes with the oven door open slightly.
This allows the rice and the potatoes time to absorb all the delicious juices.
Serve and enjoy!

items.title: Greek Stuffed Grape Leaves
items.creator: Real Greek Recipes
ingredients: 45-50 grape leaves (fresh or use a 450 gram jar)
500 grams (1 pound) half lean ground beef and half pork
150 grams (½ cup) round grain rice (such as Arborio)
1 cup whole canned tomatoes (or diced tomatoes)
70 grams (2.4 ounces) butter (diced and at room temperature)
80 ml (⅓ cup) extra virgin olive oil
500 ml (2 cups) water or stock (beef, chicken, or veg)
steps: If using brined grape leaves, soak them in a bowl with cold water for 10 minutes.
Then drain them in a strainer.
If using fresh leaves, cook them in plenty of boiling water with 3-4 tablespoons of vinegar (red wine or white vinegar) for 2 minutes.
Transfer to a bowl with ice-cold water to cool, then drain in a strainer.In both cases, trim any stems at the base of the leaves.
Add the ground meat, rice, canned tomatoes, tomato paste, and butter to a large mixing bowl.
Season with salt and pepper.
Knead the mixture well for a couple of minutes until fully combined.
Make sure to break up the butter as you go.
Take a grape leaf and lay it flat on your palm with its smooth side facing down.
Add a spoonful of the filling to the center of the leaf.
Overlap the bottom edge to partly cover the filling.
Then fold inwards, the right and left sides.
Fold on top 2 more times the remaining part of the leaf to create a hexagon.
Please See Notes Below.
Lay a couple of grape leaves to cover the bottom of a cooking pot.
Arrange the stuffed grape leaves on top, securely close together, with seam side down.
Ideally, no more than 2 layers.
Pour the hot water or stock.
Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and simmer over low heat for about 1 hour.
Then open the lid slightly on the side and cook for about 30 minutes more until there's a thin layer of liquid left in the pot.
Whisk together the ⅓ cup of olive oil and ⅓ cup lemon juice.
Pour most of it over the grape leaves and save some to drizzle on top when serving.
Allow them to sit in the pot for at least 30 minutes before serving.
Serve drizzled with olive oil and lemon, and some Greek yogurt on the side if you like.

items.title: Ali Nazik Kebab
items.creator: Give Recipe
ingredients: 5-6 chili peppers (optional (We use chili peppers, but Turkish sivri bibers are the traditional choice if you can find them.))
½ teaspoon pul biber ((use Aleppo pepper or regular red pepper flakes if you can't find pul biber))
30 g / 2 tablespoons butter ((or more if you want))
steps: Preheat the oven to 230°C (450°F).
Pierce the eggplants all over with a knife or fork.
Pierce the peppers in 1-2 places too.
Place them on an oven rack (or an oven grill) or on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
Roast for about 15 minutes, or until the peppers are cooked and have a few charred spots.
After 15 minutes, remove the peppers from the oven and turn the eggplants over.
Continue roasting for another 25-30 minutes, or until they are very soft.
While the eggplants are roasting, heat a large skillet over high heat.
Add the diced lamb in a single layer and cook for 3-4 minutes without stirring.
If you're using a stainless steel pan, don't force the lamb if it sticks.
Wait until it releases naturally, then stir.
Make sure every piece is turned.
Cook the other side for about 3 minutes.
Add the olive oil and reduce the heat to medium.
Cook for 2 more minutes, stirring occasionally.
If the lamb releases too much liquid, increase the heat so the liquid evaporates.
Add the salt, paprika, and pul biber.
Stir to combine.
By this point, the lamb should be tender.
Check a piece to make sure.
If it isn't tender enough yet, cook it a little longer.
Lower the heat if needed to prevent it from drying out.
Add the butter and let it melt completely.
Give everything a final stir, then remove the pan from the heat.
Check the eggplants after about 25 minutes (about 40 minutes total).
They should be very soft.
If not, roast them for another 5 minutes.
Let the eggplants cool until they're easy to handle.
Use a knife to scrape the flesh away from the skin.
Remove any large dark seeds.
Transfer the eggplant flesh to a strainer.
Press with the back of a spoon to remove as much liquid as possible.
This gives the mixture a better texture and helps keep the color lighter.
Finely chop the drained eggplant.
In a medium bowl, combine the strained yogurt, garlic, and salt.
Mix well.
Add the finely chopped eggplant and stir until well combined.
Taste and add more yogurt and salt if you like.
Spread the eggplant mixture onto a serving plate.
Smooth the top with the back of a spoon.

items.title: Purslane Salad (Semizotu Salatasi)
items.creator: Give Recipe
ingredients: 35 g walnuts (roughly chopped, plus extra for garnish)
steps: Trim off the thick, root ends of the purslane stems.
Wash the purslane thoroughly in plenty of cold water, drain well and roughly chop it.
Place the purslane in a large salad bowl.
Add the parsley, red onion, cherry tomatoes and walnuts.
In a small bowl or jar, whisk together the olive oil, lemon juice, pomegranate molasses and salt until well combined.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss gently until everything is evenly coated.
Sprinkle with a few extra chopped walnuts before serving.
For the best flavor, chill the salad in the refrigerator for 15–20 minutes before serving.

items.title: Quick Turkish Pogaca with Dill (Dereotlu Pogaca)
items.creator: Give Recipe
ingredients: 30 g fresh dill (washed, thoroughly dried (about 3/4 cup when chopped and loosely packed))
100 ml light olive oil or sunflower oil (⅓ cup + 1 tablespoon)
100 g plain yogurt (about ⅓ cup + 1 tablespoon)
1 medium egg white (reserve the yolk for the egg wash)
500 g plain flour (also known as all-purpose flour (about 4 cups, spooned and leveled))
200 g feta cheese or Turkish white cheese (beyaz peynir, crumbled (7 oz))
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Finely chop the dill and set it aside.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the softened butter, oil, yogurt, whole egg, egg white, vinegar, sugar, salt, and baking powder.
Mix well with a spatula.
Add the flour.
Mix with the spatula first, then use your hand to bring the dough together.
Mix just until everything holds together and you have a soft, non-sticky dough.
Don't overwork it.
Gently mix in the chopped dill until it is evenly distributed throughout the dough.
Divide the dough into 24 equal pieces (about 40 g each) and roll them into balls.
Flatten one dough ball on a work surface with your fingers.
Place some crumbled cheese (about 1½ teaspoons) in the center, then bring the edges together and pinch to seal.
Place it seam-side down on the prepared baking sheet.
Repeat with the remaining dough.
Mix the egg yolk and milk with a fork, then brush the tops of the pogacas with the egg wash.
Sprinkle with the sesame seeds and nigella seeds.
Bake for 25–30 minutes, or until the tops and bottoms are golden brown.
Check after 25 minutes.
If the bottoms are golden, they're ready.
Baking them for the full 30 minutes gives them a little more crispness.
Transfer the pogacas to a wire rack and let them cool slightly before serving.
Store them in a metal tin or a container that isn't completely airtight.
If you're using a container with a tight-fitting lid, leave it slightly ajar to allow a little airflow.

items.title: Sucuk and Eggs (Sucuklu Yumurta)
items.creator: Give Recipe
ingredients: ¼ teaspoon salt (only for the eggs)
½ teaspoon red pepper flakes ((pul biber), optional)
steps: Peel the outer casing off the sucuk and slice it into thin rounds, about ½ cm (¼ inch) thick.
Melt the butter in a shallow pan over medium heat.
Place the sucuk slices in a single layer and fry for about 30-40 seconds.
Flip the sucuk slices and cook the other side for another 30 seconds.
Make small spaces between the sucuk slices and crack the eggs into the pan.
Sprinkle the salt over the eggs only.
Use a spoon or a spatula to gently move the egg whites around a little so they cook more evenly.
Cook until the egg whites are set and the yolks are cooked to your liking.
We usually keep the yolks soft and runny.
Remove from the heat and serve immediately with fresh bread on the side.
Optionally sprinkle red pepper flakes and thyme or oregano before serving.

items.title: Sultan Mezesi
items.creator: Turkish Foodie
ingredients: 1/6 bunch of parsley leaves (washed, drained and finely chopped)
steps: Cook the LentilsRinse the red lentils thoroughly and drain.
Place them in a pot with 2 cups of water and bring to a boil.
Cook until the lentils begin to soften.
Simmer Until CreamyOnce they’re partially cooked, cover the pot and reduce the heat to low.
Let the lentils simmer gently, stirring occasionally, until all the water is absorbed and they turn into a soft, purée-like texture.
Sauté the Onion and GarlicWhile the lentils are simmering, heat 4 tablespoons of olive oil in a separate frying pan.
Add the diced onions and sauté until golden.
Then add the crushed garlic and cook for another 30 seconds, just until fragrant.
Mix It All TogetherAdd the cooked lentils to the onion and garlic mixture.
Season with salt to taste and add a few drops of lemon juice.
Stir well to combine all the flavors and remove from heat.
Prepare the ToppingIn a small saucepan, heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil.
Add the pine nuts and toast them until they turn lightly golden.
Stir in the red pepper flakes and let it sizzle for a few seconds, then remove from heat.
Serve with a Finishing TouchSpoon the lentil purée onto a serving plate.
Drizzle the pine nut and pepper topping generously over it.
Finish with a sprinkle of chopped parsley.
Serve warm or at room temperature and enjoy this elegant, comforting meze.

items.title: Sunchokes with Olive Oil
items.creator: Turkish Foodie
ingredients: 500 gram Sunchokes (peel and cut into large chunks)
steps: First, wash the Sunchokes, peel them and cut them into large chunks.
Then, place water and lemon juice in a bowl and soak the sunchokes chunks to the water and lemon juice mix for 5 minutes to prevent them getting darker and set a side.
Bring the heat to medium level.
Place the olive oil to the skillet and add carrot slices, garlic and shallots and then saute for 3 minutes.

Remove the Sunchokes chunks from water and lemon juice mix and place them on a paper towel to remove access water and then add the sunchokes to the carrot, garlic, and shallots mix and saute for 2 minutes.
Add the 500ml water, 1 fresh orange juice, 1/2 lemon juice, salt, sugar and flour to the skillet and close the skillet lid.
Then let them all cook for about 20 minutes at low heat.
Remove the dish from heat and place it to a serving plate and add finely chopped dill on top of it.
Serve cold.

items.title: Chicken Recipe
items.creator: Turkish Foodie
ingredients: 1 lbs Chicken thighs (boneless, skinless) (washed, drained and cube cut)
1/2 bunch Parsley (washed, drained and finely chopped)
2 Sweet green chili peppers (center seeds removed and thin sliced)
1 teaspoon Ground red chili pepper powder
steps: Mix parsley, onion, salt, and sumac in a bowl and set it aside.
Place the cube cut chicken thighs in a skillet and boil them with its own juice until the chicken thigh cubes' color turns to a light beige color.
(Pre-boiling helps to maintain the chicken thighs flavor.)
Heat the wok at medium heat and add the 4 tablespoons of cottonseed oil.
Place the pre-boiled chicken thigh cubes into the wok and fry them for about 4 minutes.
While frying them add a splash of water a few times (2 times) to protect the chicken thigh cubes' tenderness.
Add the sliced sweet green chili peppers and stir for about 3 minutes.
Add the ground red pepper and stir for about 2 minutes.
Add the diced tomatoes and stir for about 5 minutes.
Bring the heat to low and place the lavash bread on top of the dish to absorb the dish juice.
And keep lavash bread on top of the dish for about 30 seconds.
Let it absorb dish juice a bit.
Remove the lavash bread from the top of the dish and place on a plate.
Place the cooked chicken thigh cubes in the center of the lavash bread and distribute it evenly from top to bottom like a stripline by using a spoon.
Add the raw onions, sumac, and parsley mix on top.
Roll the lavash bread and make a wrap. (Don't forget to close the bottom of the roll.
Otherwise, all ingredients fall).
Repeat the same process until all the dish in the wok finish.
Serve.

items.title: Spinach and Poached Egg
items.creator: Turkish Foodie
ingredients: 500 gr fresh spinach leaves (washed and drained)
steps: In a saute pan, heat the olive oil, then sauté the onions over medium heat for 3-5 minutes until they become soft and translucent.
Add the spinach leaves to the saute pan and allow it to gently wilt for 1-2 minutes, giving it a delicate stir occasionally and then season the mixture with salt and pepper.
Create three (3) empty spot in the spinach mixture and drop the onions to these spots.
Cook the eggs until the whites are fully set while keeping the yolks delightfully soft.
If desired, sprinkle a touch of red pepper flakes over the eggs.
Serve

items.title: Tarator
items.creator: Turkish Foodie
ingredients: 2 Pinch of fresh dill (washed, drained and chopped)
steps: Combine strained yogurt, minced garlic, and salt in a wide bowl.
Place olive oil in a non-stick pan and add the finely chopped purple cabbages and saute for 5 minutes.
Place the sauteed purple cabbages into the yogurt mix and then add the fresh half-lemon juice and combine all well.
Place the mix on a serving plate, and add the chopped fresh dills on top.
Serve

items.title: Beyti Kebab
items.creator: Turkish Foodie
ingredients: 800 gram Ground beef (80% lean and 20% fat)
8 Thin flour tortillas (25-30cm in diameter each)
350 gram Whole milk or strained yogurt
steps: In a large bowl, place the ground beef, breadcrumbs, grated onion, beaten egg, finely pressed garlic, salt, ground cumin, red pepper flakes, and ground black pepper and combine all very well.
And then cover the bowl with stretch film and let the mixture rest and settle in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Have a small bowl of water with a drizzle of olive oil to prevent the kofte mix stick to your hands while shaping the kofte rolls.
Preheat the fan oven to 180C/350F.
Place baking paper on a large baking pan and set aside.
Dip your hand in the oily water and take about a small apple size of kofte mixture in your palm and then log roll it for about 12 cm length and gently pat to flatten.
Repeat this until the all kofte mixture end and place them side by side on the baking tray with about 3-4cm space between them.
You will have a total of 10 Beyti kofte rolls.
Bake the kofte rolls in the preheated oven for about 25 minutes.
Once Beyti kofte rolls are baked, take out the baking tray from the oven and reduce the oven temperature down to 160C fan.
Place the Beyti kofte rolls one by one on a large plate and set aside.
Place and pat the thin flour tortillas over the Beyti kofte tray, for the tortillas, to soak up the kofte juice and then place them on a dry and clean surface.
Place 2 (two) Beyti kofte rolls end to end to each thin dough tortilla to make one long roll.
Roll them tightly with a log roll shape.
Then cut the log rolls into 4 or 5 equal pieces.
Place a clean baking paper on the baking tray and place this Beyti rolls seam-side down to the baking tray.
Repeat this until all remaining kofte rolls finish.
Brush the top of the tortilla rolls with a little olive oil.
And bake them for about 5 minutes.
This will make tortilla rolls crispy.
While the Beyti kofte rolls are baking, you need to start to prepare the tomato sauce.
Pour in olive oil over a frying pan and put chopped garlic.
Sauté for about one minute on medium heat.
And then add the grated tomatoes and tomato paste and ground red pepper and combine them all well.
Simmer on medium to low heat for about 3 minutes.
After you finish the tomato sauce now it is time to make the garlic yogurt mix.
Combine the chopped garlic with the yogurt and set aside at room temperature.
Now it is time to arrange the Beyti kebab plate.
Remove the baked rolls from the oven and place the Beyti rolls in a circle shape on a serving plate and place the garlic yogurt mix in the middle of the plate.
Drizzle tomato sauce over the Beyti rolls and over the garlic yogurt.
Garnish with chopped parsley
Serve.

items.title: Patatas aliñadas con cebolla, perejil y bonito en olla exprés. Receta fácil y rápida
items.creator: Belén Otero
ingredients: 180 g de bonito del norte en aceite de oliva
90 ml de aceite de oliva virgen extra
30 ml de vinagre de Jerez o vinagre de vino blanco
500 ml de agua para la olla
steps: Pelamos y cortamos las patatas en dados de tamaño regular.
Colocamos el agua en la olla exprés Fissler y añadimos una hoja de laurel si nos apetece.
Ponemos las patatas en el cestillo de vapor, si lo tenemos, o directamente en la olla sobre el agua.
No hace falta cubrirlas por completo, porque la presión y el vapor se encargan de hacer el trabajo.
Si usamos el cestillo pondremos un trozo de papel de horno para evitar que las patatas se queden pegadas por el almidón.
Lavamos los huevos y los colocamos junto a las patatas, preferiblemente en la parte superior o en el cestillo.
Así aprovechamos la cocción y ahorramos tiempo.
Cerramos la olla correctamente, comprobando que la tapa queda bien encajada.
Es importante que el cestillo no quede muy pegado al borde, ya que podría encasquillarse y evitar que podamos abrir la tapa con normalidad.
Ponemos la olla a fuego alto hasta que alcance la presión máxima.
Cuando el indicador marque el nivel adecuado, bajamos el fuego para mantener una cocción estable.
La idea no es que la olla resople sin parar, sino que trabaje tranquila, que para nervios ya tenemos el grupo de vecinos.
Si estamos utilizando el cestillo, cocinamos durante 10 minutos, ya que al cocinarse tanto las patatas como los huevos al vapor, necesitan más tiempo.
Si las cocinamos en el agua, con 4-5 minutos debería ser suficiente.
Retiramos la olla del fuego y dejamos que pierda presión de forma natural unos minutos.
Abrimos siempre con cuidado y sin forzar la tapa.
Sacamos los huevos y los pasamos a un bol con agua fría con hielo.
Retiramos las patatas y comprobamos el punto pinchándolas con un cuchillo fino o palillo.
Deben estar tiernas, pero no deshechas; si entra limpio y sin resistencia, están listas.
Ponemos las patatas templadas en una fuente amplia.
Añadimos sal y el vinagre.
Mezclamos con mucho cuidado para que el aliño empiece a entrar en la patata sin romperla demasiado.
Incorporamos el aceite de oliva virgen extra poco a poco.
Removemos con una cuchara grande, levantando la patata desde abajo hacia arriba.
Este paso hay que hacerlo con cariño, porque una patata bien cocida se rompe si la tratamos como si estuviéramos mezclando cemento.
Pelamos los huevos cocidos y los cortamos en cuartos o en trozos grandes.
Picamos la cebolleta en juliana fina o en daditos, según nos guste encontrarla.
Si la cebolla tiene mucha fuerza, podemos dejarla 10 minutos en agua fría con una pizca de sal y luego escurrirla muy bien.
Picamos el perejil fresco justo antes de añadirlo.
Lo incorporamos a la fuente junto con la cebolleta.
Mezclamos de nuevo con suavidad para repartir el verde y el crujiente por toda la ensalada.
Escurrimos el bonito del norte, reservando un poco de su aceite si es de buena calidad.
Lo añadimos en lascas grandes por encima.
Si usamos ese aceite reservado, ponemos solo una cucharadita para no engrasar demasiado el conjunto.
Añadimos los huevos cocidos y un poco de pimienta negra si nos gusta.
Probamos el punto de sal, vinagre y aceite.
Las patatas aliñadas tienen que estar sabrosas, pero equilibradas; no buscamos que el vinagre nos despierte hasta la infancia.
Tapamos la fuente y dejamos reposar 20 o 30 minutos a temperatura ambiente si la vamos a comer pronto.
Si hace calor o vamos a tardar más, la guardamos en la nevera.
La sacamos unos minutos antes de servir para que no esté helada y la patata recupere sabor.

items.title: Baked Feta Pasta recipe
items.creator: Eli K. Giannopoulos
ingredients: 1/2 tsp Aleppo pepper or 1/4 tsp dried chilli flakes
large handful fresh basil or dill, or a mixture
steps: Preheat the oven to 180C.
In a large baking dish, toss together the cherry tomatoes, olive oil, Aleppo pepper, 1/2 tsp salt, salt a good grind of black pepper, and the garlic cloves, peeled.
Place the block of feta in the middle, turning it over so it is well coated in the oil mixture.
Bake for 40-50 minutes, until the feta is slightly charred, the tomatoes and split and soft, and the garlic cloves are tender.
Halfway through cooking, cook the pasta in a large pan of boiling, salted water as per the packets instructions.
Start checking for doneness around the 12 minute mark.
Reserve a little of the cooking water before draining the pasta and returning to the cooking pot.
Slice the basil, or chop the dill.
With a fork, crush the garlic cloves before scraping everything in the baking dish into the cooked pasta.
Stir, and add a splash of cooking water to help bring the sauce together to your desired consistency.
If the sauce becomes too loose, simply return the hot to the heat, stirring the pasta until it has reduced.
Fold in the fresh herbs just before serving.

items.title: Greek Lemon Chicken soup with Orzo (Avgolemono)
items.creator: Eli K. Giannopoulos
ingredients: 6 skin on bone in chicken thighs
small handful fresh dill, roughly chopped
steps: Place the chicken thighs in a large pot with the red onion, peeled and halved, and the carrots, peeled and finely chopped.
Season well and add the water, adding more if needed to make sure the chicken pieces are completely covered.
Bring to the boil before reducing the heat to low.
Allow to simmer with the lid on for 30 minutes.
Remove the chicken thighs from the pan and set aside.
Check the seasoning and add more salt and pepper to the soup if needed.
Add the orzo and turn the heat up to medium.
Cook with the lid on for another 15 minutes, or until the pasta is just tender.
Meanwhile, once the chicken is cool enough to touch discard the skins and shred the meat from the bone, returning the bones to the pot as soon as you can.
Once the orzo is tender, remove the chicken bones and red onion, and remove 3-4 ladles of hot soup from the pot into a jug, using a sieve to leave any carrot or orzo pieces behind.
Whisk the eggs until just frothy and then whisk in the lemon juice.
Whisking constantly, slowly pour the hot soup into the egg mixture until loose, light and creamy.
Then slowly whisk it back into the soup pot.
Return the shredded chicken to the soup.
Add a little more water if needed, and check the seasoning again.
Once the chicken has warmed through remove from the heat and stir through the chopped dill before serving.

items.title: How to make Greek Yogurt (Homemade Greek Yogurt recipe)
items.creator: Eli K. Giannopoulos
steps: Pre-heat the oven to 40 degrees celsius / 104 fahrenheit.
Line a large casserole or dutch oven large enough to hold a glass mixing bowl that will hold all the milk with clean dish towels.
Heat the milk over a medium high heat in a large saucepan, stirring almost constantly with a heatproof spatula to make sure the milk does not burn on the bottom of the pan.
Bring the milk to somewhere between 82-88 degrees Celsius / 180-190 Fahrenheit, measured with a sugar thermometer.
Heat the milk for 5 minutes, stirring constantly, and adjusting the heat if necessary to keep it within the correct temperature range.
Pour the milk into your glass bowl and allow to cool to between 41-45 degrees celsius / 105-110 fahrenheit.
Add your 2 tablespoons of “seed” yoghurt to the lukewarm milk.
Transfer the bowl to the dish towel lined casserole and transfer to the pre-heated oven.
Leave for at least 8 hours until the yogurt has reached a consistency slightly looser than natural yogurt.
Cover with kitchen wrap and chill in the fridge overnight.
Remove the yogurt from the fridge, it should have thickened slightly and it should taste rich, creamy and pleasantly tangy.
Use a large rubber band to secure a piece of cheesecloth over the top of another clean glass bowl or wide mouthed jug.
Allow just enough give in the cheesecloth to allow you to scrape the yogurt into the indentation.
Return to the fridge and allow to strain for at least 2 hours to reach the consistency of Greek yogurt – the exact timings will rely on the amount of whey in your yogurt and personal preference.
Transfer to a clean air tight tub or container and consume within 7 days.

items.title: Greek marinade for chicken
items.creator: Eli K. Giannopoulos
ingredients: 3 tbsp Greek yogurt (or the juice of 1 lemon)
500g chicken thighs, breasts, or other chicken pieces, skin on or off (1 lb 1 1/2 oz)
steps: In a large bowl or ziplock bag combine the oil, lemon zest, garlic cloves, peeled and crushed, Greek yogurt (or the juice of the lemon, if you don’t have any Greek yogurt to hand), dried oregano, honey, red wine vinegar, salt and plenty of black pepper.
Whisk to combine.
Add your choice of chicken pieces and marinate in the fridge for at least two hours, but preferably overnight.
In a 200 degrees (390 fahrenheit) oven roast the chicken pieces for 20-30 minutes depending on their size (40 minutes for bone in chicken thighs) until the meat is cooked through.
If the pieces still have their skin, finish them under a hot grill if needed to get nice crispy skin and a good level of caramelisation.
Cook on a direct heat until the meat is caramelised before moving to the edge of the pan or an area of indirect heat to cook through.

We do not recommend the griddle pan method, only the barbecue for skin on or bone in pieces of chicken, though skin on, bone in chicken thighs can be browned in the pan before being transferred to the oven to cook through.

items.title: Greek Chickpea salad with Feta cheese
items.creator: Eli K. Giannopoulos
steps: Drain the chickpeas and rinse them until the cold tap until the water coming out the bottom runs clean.
Set aside to let any excess water drain.
Quarter the cherry tomatoes and transfer them to a large mixing bowl.
Peel the cucumber and cut into quartered slices.
Finely chop the red onion, and quarter the olives, adding the cucumber, onion and olives to the tomato bowl.
Roughly chop the fresh herbs, and add them to the bowl along with the drained chickpeas.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the olive oil and vinegar along with a generous pinch of salt and a good amount of black pepper.
Pour over the salad and stir until everything is coated in the dressing.
Crumble in the feta, and fold it into the salad carefully, making sure it is coated in the dressing but that it does not break down too much.
Check the seasoning to see if it needs any more salt and pepper, and serve.

items.title: Greek Stuffed Zucchini in Egg Lemon Sauce (Avgolemono)
items.creator: Eli K. Giannopoulos
ingredients: 1 tbsp finely chopped fresh dill, plus extra for garnishing
steps: Heat the oil in the bottom of a large skillet or frying pan set over a medium high heat and gently fry the onion, peeled and finely chopped with a pinch of salt until soft and starting to colour.
Add the beef and fry for about 10 minutes, breaking it up with the wooden spoon until it is cooked through and has browned in places.
Add the garlic, peeled and crushed along with the rice.
Cook for another minute until the garlic is aromatic and the rice grains have heated through.
Add the white wine and turn the heat down to low.
Allow the wine to bubble away completely.
Remove the pan from the heat.
Stir in the herbs, spices and a generous amount of black pepper.
Check for seasoning and set aside to cool a little.
Top and tail the zucchini and slice them into three equal pieces.
Using a very sharp knife and a long handled spoon – an ice cream spoon works well for this – or an apple corer, hollow out the zucchini pieces to create tubes with 1/2 cm (0.3 inch) sides.
Stand the zucchini up to create a honeycomb pattern in a lidded saucepan where they fit snuggly.

To make sure they stand up straight with their cut bottoms flush to the bottom of the pan, and to make sure they can’t fall over during cooking cut up pieces of potato to wedge between them to keep them upright.
Using a small spoon, fill each zucchini tube with the beef mixture.
You want this to be quite tightly packed, but not so much that the rice does not have a chance to expand.
Pour cold water into the pan so it reaches half way up the zucchini tubes and salt the water well.
Set it over a medium high heat to bring the water to the boil before turning it down to a low simmer.
Simmer for 30-40 minutes with the lid on, or until the zucchini are just tender.
Using tongs, carefully remove the zucchini from the pan, setting aside on a plate lined with kitchen paper to capture any extra moisture.
Meanwhile, whisk together the egg yolks with the cornstarch into a thick paste, and gradually whisk in the lemon juice.
Set aside.
Strain the remaining cooking liquid and slowly whisk 200ml (2/3 cup) into the egg mixture.
Pour the mixture into the saucepan and return it to the low heat.
Warm through the egg sauce, whisking often until it has thickened substantially, and will coat the stuffed zucchini when poured over the top.
Serve the stuffed zucchini warm or at room temperature with the freshly made sauce poured over the top and with an extra sprinkling of fresh dill.

items.title: Quesillo Canario: Canarian Style Flan
items.creator: Spanish Sabores
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Butter a flan pan or baking mold and set it aside.
Pour the granulated sugar and the water into a heavy-based saucepan and set it over medium heat.
Stir until the sugar has dissolved, then stop stirring and bring the mixture to a boil.
Let it cook until the sugar has turned a rich golden brown, being careful not to let it burn.
Immediately pour the hot caramel into the buttered flan pan and turn it so the base and sides of the pan are coated in caramel.
Work quickly before it hardens!
Beat the eggs well, and then whisk in the condensed milk and vanilla until the mixture is combined.
Beat in the whole milk and lemon zest.
Pour the egg and milk mixture into the flan mold, and place in a large roasting pan.
Create the bain marie by filling it with enough boiling water to go halfway up the side of the flan mold.
Bake the quesillo at 350°F (175°C) for about 35-50 minutes, or until it has an internal temperature of 175°F (79°C).
The baking time will depend on the pan you are using, so after about 35 minutes, check it frequently.
Let the flan cool completely; preferably, chill it in the fridge overnight or for at least 4 hours.
When you're ready to serve the quesillo, run a knife around the edge, then place a serving plate over the pan, flip it over, and carefully remove the pan.
The flan should easily come out.
Serve with some caramel sauce and enjoy!

items.title: Pumpkin Flan (Flan de Calabaza)
items.creator: Spanish Sabores
steps: Stir the water and granulated sugar in a saucepan over medium heat until it's dissolved, then stop stirring.
Let the mixture boil until it turns a rich golden brown.
This will take several minutes, but watch it closely so it doesn't burn.
Be sure not to stir it after the sugar is dissolved, or the caramel will crystallize.
Once the caramel is ready, quickly pour it into a 4 1/2 cup baking mold and swirl the caramel around to make sure that it coats the bottom and sides of the mold before it hardens.
Preheat the oven to 325°F (163°C).
Pour the milk, sugar, pumpkin purée, spices, and vanilla into a saucepan and whisk over medium heat until simmering.
Cook until all of the sugar is dissolved and the mixture is heated through.
Remove the mixture from the heat and let it cool for about 10 minutes, stirring every minute or two.
Lightly beat the eggs in a large bowl.
Making sure that the milk and pumpkin mixture is sufficiently cool so that it won't scramble the eggs, whisk in this mixture little by little until it all is incorporated.
Pour the custard mixture into the prepared mold.
Place the flan mold into a large roasting pan with deep sides.
Fill the roasting pan with enough water to go halfway up the sides of the flan mold to create a bain marie.
This ensures that the flan will cook evenly without cracking.
Bake the flan at 325°F (163°C) for about 1 hour, or until it jiggles slightly and has an internal temperature of 175°F (79°C).
Remove the mold from the pan of water and allow it to cool completely.
Cover with plastic wrap and let chill in the fridge overnight, or for at least 4 hours.
When you're ready to serve the flan, run a knife around the edges of the mold.
Place the serving dish on top, and quickly flip the flan over.
Lift off the mold and the flan should slide right out, covered in a golden caramel sauce.
Enjoy the pumpkin flan on its own, or with whipped cream!

items.title: Langoustine & Prawn Ravioli with Manzanilla
items.creator: Spanish Sabores
ingredients: 6 large raw prawns (peeled, deveined, and roughly chopped)
12 ravioli wrappers (for 6 closed ravioli (3 per person))
1/8 cup manzanilla wine (such as Bodega Barbadillo Manzanilla Solear)
steps: Place half of the chopped prawns, heavy cream, egg white, and lemon zest into a food processor.
Lightly pulse the mixture into a thick paste, then season with salt and pepper and mix in the remaining chopped prawns.
Fill each ravioli with about a tablespoon of filling, being careful not to over or under fill.
Seal the edges with some water or egg, then tightly crimp the edges with a fork so that they don't open when cooking.
Leave on a lightly floured plate, and bring a large pot of water to a boil.
To prepare the sauce, slowly melt the butter in a heavy pan, and add the langoustines (cigalas).
Poach them in the butter by spooning the hot butter over them constantly.
It should take about 2 minutes to cook them through, then remove them immediately and let them rest on a plate.
Add the garlic to the butter and slowly simmer for about one minute.
Make sure the heat is low so that the garlic doesn't color.
Add the juice from half of a small lemon and about 1/8 cup of manzanilla wine.
Turn up the heat and let it reduce for about 30 seconds, then stir in the capers.
Take the pan off the heat.
To cook the ravioli, gently drop them into a large pot of boiling salted water.
Allow them to boil for 1-2 minutes, depending upon their wrappers.
Remove with a slotted spoon and place on the serving dish. (I've portioned 3 per person in this recipe.)
Reheat the sauce, then add the langoustines and coat them in the sauce.
Pour the sauce on top of the ravioli and top with a poached langoustine.
Serve immediately and pair with a cold glass of manzanilla!

items.title: Chorizo and White Bean Stew with Spinach
items.creator: Spanish Sabores
ingredients: 4 links fresh chorizo or other Spanish sausage (cut into chunks)
1 can diced tomatoes (or a freshly diced medium tomato)
2 cans large white beans (alubias extras) (drained and rinsed)
steps: Warm the butter and oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onions and sauté the onions until they are just browning, about 10 minutes.
Add the diced garlic and sauté another minute.
Add the fresh chorizo and let the chunks brown on each side.
Add the carrot, semi cured chorizo, herbs, and cayenne pepper and stir well, then pour in the white wine and simmer for 1 minute to reduce the wine.
Add the chopped tomatoes and tomato paste, and simmer for 2 minutes.
Add the 3 cups of chicken stock, then bring to a simmer and cook for 15 minutes uncovered.
Add in the fresh spinach and beans, then cover and cook for 10 minutes.
Serve hot and enjoy!

items.title: Spanish Baked Rice with Garbanzos and Dates
items.creator: Spanish Sabores
ingredients: 1/2 cup cherry tomatoes (sliced in half lengthwise)
2 1/2 cups vegetable stock (or chicken stock for a non-vegetarian version)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Sauté the onion in two tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil until caramelized.
Add the minced garlic for 30 seconds, then add half of the chopped dried fruits and sauté for 2 minutes.
Mix in the tomato paste and cherry tomatoes, then add the vegetable stock, chickpeas, paprika, and salt.
Bring to a boil, then stir in the rice.
Slice about 1/4 inch off the top of the head of garlic to expose the tops of the garlic cloves.
Place the head of garlic in the center of the pan, sprinkle the rest of the dried fruits on top of the rice, and drizzle with about a tablespoon of olive oil.
Bake the rice dish for 30 minutes at 400°F (200°C).
In the meantime, brown the almonds in a hot frying pan (with a touch of olive oil if you wish).
Be sure to stir them constantly, and don't let them burn!
Top the finished dish with the toasted almonds and enjoy while it's hot and fresh.

items.title: Spanish Clams with Chorizo in Garlic Sauce
items.creator: Spanish Sabores
steps: Place a large pot over medium heat, then pour in the olive oil and heat up.
Add the onion and sauté until it's soft and translucent, about 3-4 minutes.
Add the chorizo and continue to cook until enough fat has released to coat the onion, about 3 minutes.
Add the garlic and paprika to the pot, then stir and sauté until aromatic, about 1 minute.
Pour the white wine into the pot, then bring to a boil.
Add the clams to the pot, making sure they're evenly distributed, then cover with a lid and cook until the clams have opened up, about 6-7 minutes.
Discard any that do not open.
Remove the pot from heat and stir in the parsley and butter.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve the clams hot in bowls with slices of crusty bread, and enjoy!

items.title: Amaretto-Croissants
items.creator: Dominique
ingredients: 1 Rolle Croissantteig (aus dem Kühlregal, ca. 275 g)
steps: Heize den Backofen auf 190 °C Ober-/Unterhitze vor und lege ein Backblech mit Backpapier aus.
Rolle den Croissantteig aus und trenne die einzelnen Dreiecke an den vorgegebenen Markierungen.
Verrühre für die Füllung die gemahlenen Mandeln mit 2 EL Amaretto, dem Mandelextrakt und 1 EL Zucker zu einer streichfähigen Masse.
Verteile etwas von der Mandelmasse auf dem breiten Ende der Teigdreiecke.
Rolle die Dreiecke von der breiten Seite zur Spitze hin auf und forme sie zu Hörnchen.
Verquirle das Eigelb mit dem Wasser und bestreiche die Croissants damit.
Backe die vorbereiteten Croissants etwa 15-18 Minuten, bis sie goldbraun und knusprig sind.
Gib währenddessen 20 g Zucker und 30 ml Amaretto in einen kleinen Topf und erhitze die Mischung unter gelegentlichem Rühren, bis sich der Zucker vollständig aufgelöst hat.
Röste die Mandelblättchen in einer Pfanne ohne zusätzliches Fett 2-3 Minuten goldbraun an.
Bestreiche die noch warmen Croissants direkt nach dem Backen mit dem Amaretto-Sirup.
Streue sofort die gerösteten Mandelblättchen darüber.
Lass die Croissants auskühlen und bestäube sie je nach Geschmack vor dem Servieren mit Puderzucker.

items.title: Himbeer-Iced-Americano
items.creator: Julia Erin
steps: Für den Himbeersirup: Gib Himbeeren, Wasser und Zucker in einen kleinen Topf.
Bring alles unter gelegentlichem Rühren leicht zum Köcheln.
Lass die Mischung 10-15 Minuten sanft köcheln und zerdrücke dabei die Himbeeren leicht.
Nimm den Topf vom Herd und lass alles 10 Minuten ziehen.
Danach, seihe den Sirup durch ein feines Sieb ab.
Rühre den Zitronensaft ein und lass den Sirup vollständig abkühlen.
Gib für den Himbeer-Iced-Americano den Himbeersirup in ein großes Glas und fülle das Glas mit Eiswürfeln.
Gieße kaltes Wasser dazu und gieße die frisch gezogenen Espresso-Shots langsam über das Eis.
Rühre nach Belieben um und garniere mit frischen Himbeeren.

items.title: Grilled Cheese Sandwich mit schwarzen Bohnen
items.creator: Olivia
steps: Gib die Bohnen in eine kleine Schüssel und zerstampfe sie grob.
Würze die Bohnen mit Salz, Pfeffer, Kreuzkümmel, Paprikapulver und Limettensaft, vermische alles gut.
Bestreiche die Außenseite der Sauerteigbrotscheiben mit Butter.
Lege eine Scheibe mit der Butterseite nach unten in eine heiße Pfanne.
Verteile etwas Gouda und Emmentaler auf das Brot, gib dann die gewürzten Bohnen darauf.
Streue Koriander und optional Jalapeños darüber.
Belege mit dem restlichen Käse.
Lege die zweite Brotscheibe mit der Butterseite nach oben darauf.
Brate das Sandwich bei mittlerer Hitze beidseitig goldbraun, bis der Käse geschmolzen ist.
Schneide das Sandwich auf und serviere es warm.

items.title: Coconut Chicken Curry With Tomatoes and Corn
items.creator: Ali Slagle
ingredients: 3 tablespoons coconut or neutral oil, such as avocado
1 ½ to 2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 pint cherry or other small tomatoes
2 ears of corn, kernels removed and cobs reserved (or 2 cups frozen, unthawed kernels)
Cooked rice, cilantro and/or lime wedges, for serving
steps: In a large Dutch oven over medium, heat the oil.
Add the onion, garlic, ginger and a pinch of salt.
Cook, stirring occasionally, until the onion is softened, 6 to 8 minutes.
Meanwhile, in a medium bowl, sprinkle the chicken with the curry powder and 2 teaspoons Diamond Crystal kosher salt.
Stir to coat.
Add the chicken to the pot.
Cook, stirring occasionally, until the chicken loses its raw color, 6 to 8 minutes.
Add the coconut milk and tomatoes. (It’s OK if the chicken isn’t submerged.) Snap the reserved corn cobs in half, if using, and add to the pot as well.
Bring to a boil over medium-high, then reduce heat and simmer, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is tender and the curry has thickened, 17 to 20 minutes.
Remove the corn cobs.
Stir in the corn kernels and simmer until bright and crisp-tender, 3 to 5 minutes.
Taste the curry, and salt to taste.
Serve with rice, cilantro and a squeeze of lime.

items.title: Masala Chicken and Chickpeas
items.creator: Kay Chun
ingredients: ½ cup plain whole milk Greek yogurt
1 cup loosely-packed, coarsely-chopped cilantro leaves and tender stems, plus 2 tablespoons finely chopped, divided
2 tablespoons neutral oil, such as safflower, divided
1 cup finely chopped onion (from ½ onion)
½ teaspoon kashmiri chile powder (or ¼ teaspoon cayenne plus ¼ teaspoon sweet paprika)
1 pound ground chicken, preferably dark meat
½ cup canned chickpeas, rinsed and drained
4 ounces baby spinach, coarsely chopped (about 4 cups)
Cooked basmati rice and lime wedges, for serving
steps: In a food processor, combine yogurt, the coarsely chopped cilantro and water and purée, scraping down the sides and bottom of the bowl, until smooth.
(If you don’t want to use a food processor, finely chop the cilantro leaves and stems by hand.
Add the chopped herbs to a small bowl with the yogurt and water and stir until smooth.) Season with salt and pepper.
In a 12-inch nonstick skillet, combine 1 tablespoon of the oil and butter over medium heat and cook until butter melts.
Add cumin seeds and stir until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add onion, season with salt and pepper and cook, stirring occasionally, until lightly golden, 5 minutes.
Add the remaining 1 tablespoon oil, garlic, ginger, garam masala and chile powder and cook, stirring, until the spices are fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add tomato and cook, stirring, until tomato breaks down and mixture is saucy, 3 minutes.
Add chicken, season with salt and pepper and cook, stirring and breaking up the meat until it is crumbly, about 3 minutes.
Add chickpeas and cook, stirring occasionally, until chicken is cooked through, 2 minutes longer.
Stir in spinach and the finely chopped cilantro until spinach is wilted.
To serve, divide chicken mixture among bowls over rice.
Drizzle with the cilantro yogurt and serve with lime wedges for squeezing over.
tags: Curry, Poultry, Beans, Dinner, Lunch, Main Course

items.title: Blue Cheese Coleslaw
items.creator: Ali Slagle
ingredients: 3 ounces crumbled blue cheese (about ½ cup), plus more for serving
¼ cup sour cream or whole-milk Greek yogurt
1 large garlic clove, finely chopped or grated
2 pounds thinly sliced green or red cabbage (about 10 cups or ½ large head – or use store bought slaw blend)
4 celery stalks, thinly sliced, plus any leaves
2 carrots, grated on the large holes of a box grater
steps: In a microwave-safe medium bowl or large liquid measuring cup, microwave the blue cheese until just warm, about 20 seconds.
Stir with a spoon to smooth, then add the buttermilk, sour cream, mayonnaise, lemon juice, garlic and a few grinds of pepper.
Stir to combine.
Season to taste with salt and pepper.
In a large bowl, toss the cabbage, celery and carrots with a pinch of salt.
Add most of the dressing and toss to coat, adding more dressing as needed to thinly coat.
Top with more black pepper and blue cheese as you like.
Serve right away, leave out for up to 2 hours, or cover and refrigerate for up to 3 days.

items.title: Air Fryer Tempeh
items.creator: The Big Man's World
steps: Slice the tempeh into 1/2 inch strips.
Steam them in the microwave for 3 minutes or in a steamer basket over hot water for 8 minutes.
Whisk together the soy sauce, maple syrup, rice vinegar, sesame oil, garlic, ginger, and smoked paprika in a bowl.
Preheat the air fryer to 380°F.
Pat dry the still-warm tempeh and add it to the marinade.
Toss to coat and let sit for 1-2 minutes.
Lift the tempeh from the marinade (reserve the excess) and arrange the strips in a single layer in the air fryer basket.
Air fry for 8 minutes, flip, brush with the excess marinade, and cook for another 4 minutes, or until caramelized and charred.
Remove from the air fryer basket and serve immediately.

items.title: Oven Baked Chicken Breast
items.creator: The Big Man's World
steps: Preheat the oven to 200C/400F.
