items.title: Keleya Zaara
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat.
Add the lamb and cook until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Season with saffron, salt and pepper to taste; stir in all but 4 tablespoons of the onion, and pour in the water.
Bring to the boil, then cover, reduce heat to medium-low, and simmer until the lamb is tender, about 15 minutes.
Uncover the pan, stir in the butter and allow the sauce reduce 5 to 10 minutes to desired consistency.
Season to taste with salt and pepper, then pour into a serving dish.
Sprinkle with the remaining chopped onions and parsley.
Garnish with lemon wedges to serve.

items.title: Cajun spiced fish tacos
steps: Cooking in a cajun spice and cayenne pepper marinade makes this fish super succulent and flavoursome.
Top with a zesty dressing and serve in a tortilla for a quick, fuss-free main that's delightfully summery.
On a large plate, mix the cajun spice and cayenne pepper with a little seasoning and use to coat the fish all over.
Heat a little oil in a frying pan, add in the fish and cook over a medium heat until golden.
Reduce the heat and continue frying until the fish is cooked through, about 10 minutes.
Cook in batches if you don’t have enough room in the pan.
Meanwhile, prepare the dressing by combining all the ingredients with a little seasoning.
Soften the tortillas by heating in the microwave for 5-10 seconds.
Pile high with the avocado, lettuce and spring onion, add a spoonful of salsa, top with large flakes of fish and drizzle over the dressing.

items.title: Purple sprouting broccoli tempura with nuoc cham
steps: For the nuoc cham, whisk together all of the ingredients with 5 tbsp hot water in a small bowl. Set aside while you make the tempura.
Whisk the cornflour, plain flour, sesame seeds (if using) and a large pinch of salt together.
Fill a large, deep pan no more than a third full with the vegetable oil and heat until it reaches 180C or a cube of bread dropped in browns in 20 seconds.
Quickly whisk the soda water into the flour mixture, being careful not to overmix, then dunk in the broccoli using tongs.
Carefully lower into the hot oil and cook for 2-3 mins until crisp.
Drain on kitchen paper, then serve with the nuoc cham on the side for dipping.

items.title: Lamb Pilaf (Plov)
steps: Place the raisins and prunes into a small bowl and pour over enough water to cover. Add lemon juice and let soak for at least 1 hour. Drain. Roughly chop the prunes.
Meanwhile, heat the butter in a large pan, add the onion, and cook for 5 minutes. Add cubed lamb, ground lamb, and crushed garlic cloves. Fry for 5 minutes, stirring constantly until browned.
Pour 2/3 cup (150 milliliters) of stock into the pan. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat, cover, and simmer for 1 hour, or until the lamb is tender.
Add the remaining stock and bring to a boil. Add rinsed long-grain white rice and a large pinch of saffron. Stir, then cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the rice is tender.
Add the drained raisins, drained chopped prunes, and salt and pepper to taste. Heat through for a few minutes, then turn out onto a warmed serving dish and garnish with sprigs of flat-leaf parsley.

items.title: Drunken noodles (pad kee mao)
steps: Prepare the noodles following pack instructions, then drain and set aside. Combine all the ingredients for the sauce in a small bowl or jug, and set aside.
Heat the oil in a large wok or frying pan over a high heat and stir-fry the garlic and chilli for 20 seconds until just starting to turn golden.
Add the steak and stir-fry for 1 minute until seared and starting to brown.
Add the broccoli and stir-fry for another minute, then tip in the noodles and add the sauce.
Stir-fry for another 1-2 mins until well combined and piping hot.
Stir through the basil and turn off the heat. Serve immediately to avoid overcooking.

items.title: Maple-Shallot Pork Tenderloin
items.creator: Kia Damon
ingredients: 1 (1½-pound) pork tenderloin, silver skin removed (see Tip)
2 teaspoons kosher salt (such as Diamond Crystal)
3 tablespoons regular or golden raisins, roughly chopped
steps: Heat the oven to 425 degrees and position a rack in the middle of the oven.
Line a sheet pan with aluminum foil and place an oven-safe wire rack in the pan.
In a small bowl, whisk together the salt, smoked paprika and garlic powder.
Pat the pork dry, then coat it in olive oil and sprinkle evenly with the seasoning blend.
Place pork on the rack in the prepared sheet pan and roast on middle rack until the internal temperature reaches 145 degrees, about 20 minutes.
While the pork is roasting, make the agrodolce: Combine the maple syrup, vinegar, shallots and raisins in a small saucepan.
Whisk well, then bring to a boil.
Once boiling, reduce the heat to maintain a simmer.
Cook, whisking occasionally, until the liquid has reduced by half, 18 to 20 minutes.
Remove from the heat.
When the pork has finished cooking, remove it from the oven and let it rest 5 minutes before slicing into ½-inch-thick rounds.
Transfer to a serving plate and top with a couple spoonfuls of the agrodolce.
Serve with the remaining sauce on the side. (Any leftover sauce is delicious on roasted fish or grilled vegetables.)

items.title: Reverse-Seared Rib-Eye Steak
items.creator: Sam Sifton
ingredients: Kosher salt (such as Diamond Crystal) and freshly ground black pepper
steps: Take your steak out of the fridge a half-hour or so before you plan to cook it, so it loses its chill.
Salt it well and, if you like, hit it with some freshly ground black pepper.
Heat the oven to 200 degrees and set a wire rack in a rimmed sheet pan.
Set the steak on the rack and roast it until its internal temperature is around 110 degrees.
That will take something between 20 to 30 minutes, but don’t use time as your guide.
Use the thermometer.
Rest the meat for 20 minutes while you light either a charcoal grill or heat a gas one until it’s ripping. (You can definitely finish the steak on a stovetop, but you’ll get a lot of smoke.)
Sear the meat to deeply brown, about 90 seconds a side, then check the temperature.
It should be in the low 120s for rare.
Rest for about 5 minutes and carve.
tags: Steaks and Chops, Dinner, Main Course

items.title: Miyan Masara (Corn Soup)
items.creator: Yewande Komolafe
ingredients: 3 medium carrots (about 6 ounces), roughly chopped (1 ½ cups)
2 tablespoons neutral oil, such as safflower, grapeseed or canola oil
1 Scotch bonnet or habanero pepper, halved, seeds in or out
2 teaspoons kosher salt (such as Diamond Crystal), more to taste
¼ cup roasted unsalted peanuts, roughly chopped
1 tablespoon fresh lime juice (from 1 fresh lime)
¼ cup plus 2 tablespoons maishanu or ghee
¼ cup crispy shallots, homemade or store-bought
steps: Prepare the stock: Shuck corn, reserving husks.
Using a paring knife, slice kernels into a medium bowl.
Set aside.
Add corn cobs, onion, carrots, celery and cold water to a large stockpot over medium-high.
Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to medium to maintain a gentle simmer.
Cook, uncovered, until vegetables are softened and liquid is three-fourths of the original volume, about 30 minutes.
Strain through a fine-mesh sieve and discard solids.
You should have about 4 cups stock.
Prepare the soup: Add oil to a large, heavy-bottomed pot and place over medium heat.
Add onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and caramelized in spots, 10 to 12 minutes.
Add garlic and Scotch bonnet, and cook until fragrant and softened, about 2 minutes.
Add 1 teaspoon salt and reserved corn kernels, stirring to coat with onion mix.
Cook until corn is bright yellow and warmed through, about 6 minutes.
Stir in remaining teaspoon salt and peanuts.
Pour in all the prepared stock, increase heat to medium-high and bring to a simmer, about 6 minutes.
Reduce heat to medium-low, and simmer gently, stirring occasionally, until the liquid reduces by one-third, about 20 minutes.
In a small pot or saucepan over low heat, melt the maishanu, 1 to 2 minutes.
Working in batches, transfer the soup to a blender.
Purée, beginning on low and gradually increasing the speed to high, until the soup is smooth, 4 minutes.
(You can also use an immersion blender for this step.) With the motor running on low, stream in half of the melted maishanu.
Pass through a fine-mesh sieve if a silky texture is desired, or leave as-is for a more rustic finish.
Season to taste with lime juice, cayenne and more salt, if necessary.
To serve, ladle hot soup into warm bowls.
Serve immediately, finishing with a drizzle of warm maishanu, a spoonful of crumbled goat cheese and a handful of crispy shallots.

items.title: Kräuter-Omelett mit Lachs und Hüttenkäse
items.creator: Kitchen Stories
steps: Schneide den Räucherlachs in kleine Würfel.
Wasche den Dill, schüttle ihn trocken, zupfe die Spitzen ab und hacke sie fein.
Lege einige Dillspitzen zum Garnieren beiseite.
Putze die Frühlingszwiebeln und schneide sie in feine Ringe.
Gib Lachs, Dill, Frühlingszwiebeln und körnigen Frischkäse in eine Schüssel.
Vermische alles gründlich und schmecke die Füllung mit Zitronensaft, etwas Salz und Pfeffer ab.
Schneide Schnittlauch, Petersilie und Thymian klein, wenn du frische Kräuter verwendest.
Tipp: Das geht besonders gut mit einer Kräuterschere 🛒.
Verquirle die Eier mit Milch.
Gib Schnittlauch, Petersilie und Thymian dazu und würze die Mischung mit Salz und Pfeffer.
Erhitze in einer Pfanne bei mittlerer Hitze etwas Butter.
Gieße ein Viertel der Eiermasse hinein und brate das Omelett zugedeckt 4–5 Minuten, bis die Unterseite leicht gebräunt und die Oberfläche gestockt ist.
Lass das Omelett auf einen Teller gleiten.
Verteile ein Viertel der Füllung auf einer Hälfte und klappe die andere Hälfte darüber.
Bereite die übrigen Omeletts auf dieselbe Weise zu, bis die Eiermasse und die Füllung aufgebraucht sind.
Richte die Omeletts auf Tellern an und garniere sie mit den restlichen Dillspitzen.

items.title: Zucchini-Cracker mit Kräutern
items.creator: Anke
ingredients: 1 EL Sesam oder Kürbiskerne (zum Bestreuen, optional)
steps: Heize den Backofen auf 175 °C Ober-/Unterhitze vor und lege ein Backblech mit Backpapier aus.
Rasple die Zucchini grob, salze sie leicht und lasse sie 10 Minuten ziehen.
Drücke anschließend möglichst viel Flüssigkeit mit einem sauberen Küchentuch aus.
Vermische die ausgedrückte Zucchini mit Hafermehl, Parmesan, Leinsamen, Eiern und Olivenöl.
Gib Knoblauchpulver, Zwiebelpulver, Oregano, Thymian, Rosmarin, Paprikapulver sowie Pfeffer dazu und verrühre alles zu einem gleichmäßigen, formbaren Teig.
Verteile den Teig auf dem Backblech und streiche ihn etwa 4–5 mm dünn zu einem Rechteck aus.
Ritze den Teig mit einem Messer oder Pizzaschneider in gleich große Quadrate oder Rechtecke ein.
Bestreue ihn nach Belieben mit Sesam oder Kürbiskernen und drücke die Körner leicht an.
Backe die Cracker 22–25 Minuten, bis sie goldbraun und knusprig sind.
Lasse die Zucchini-Cracker etwa 10 Minuten auf dem Blech abkühlen.
Brich sie anschließend entlang der eingeschnittenen Linien auseinander.

items.title: Golden-Milk-Chia-Pudding
items.creator: Olivia
ingredients: 2 EL gehackte Nüsse (z. B. Mandeln oder Walnüsse)
steps: Erwärme in einem kleinen Topf Milch mit Kurkuma, Ingwer, Zimt, Honig, einer Prise Salz und Pfeffer sowie etwas Vanilleextrakt.
Rühre die Chiasamen ein.
Fülle die Mischung in Gläser und stelle sie für mindestens 2 Stunden im Kühlschrank oder am besten über Nacht kalt, damit die Chiasamen quellen können.
Toppe den Golden-Milk-Chia-Pudding mit ein paar gehackten Nüssen und Kokosraspeln

items.title: Hafer-Nuss-Brötchen aus dem Airfryer
items.creator: Kitchen Stories
steps: Vermische Haferflocken, Leinsamen und Chiasamen mit Wasser in einer Schüssel.
Stelle sie für 2 Stunden beiseite, damit sie aufquellen können.
Gib zwei Drittel der Nüsse, den Quark, Mandelmus, Flohsamenschalen, Salz und Backpulver in eine Schüssel.
Gib die Hafer-Samen-Mischung zum Teig und verknete alles miteinander.
Möchtest du deine Brötchen später auch noch mit Nüssen bestreuen, stelle den Rest beiseite.
Sonst kannst du alle Nüsse mit in den Teig geben.
Heize die Heißluftfritteuse für 5 Minuten auf 200 °C vor.
Teile den Teig in 12 Stücke und forme sie zu Kugeln oder in eine längliche Form, je nachdem, wie deine Brötchen am Ende aussehen sollen.
Bestreiche die Oberseite jedes Brötchens mit etwas Eiweiß und wenn du magst mit der restlichen Nussmischung.
Lege 6 Hafer-Nuss-Teiglinge auf einmal in den Korb des Airfryers und backe die Brötchen für 20-25 Minuten.
Schaue zwischendurch nach, ob du sie einmal auflockern oder wenden solltest.
Wiederhole den Vorgang mit den restlichen Brötchen.

items.title: Passion Fruit Chia Pudding
items.creator: Skinnytaste
ingredients: ½ cup vanilla yogurt (I used Oikos Pro=)
2 cups passion fruit pulp (I used Pitaya Foods Passion Fruit - Seedless Cubes)
steps: Blend the tofu, yogurt, passion fruit, sweetener, and vanilla in a blender until completely smooth.
Add the chia seeds and mix well.
Refrigerate at least 4 hours, but overnight is best to allow the chia seeds to thicken the mixture.
Transfer to 5 serving dishes and top with raspberries before serving.

items.title: Chicken Broccoli Casserole
items.creator: Budget Bytes
steps: Gather ingredients.
Roughly chop the broccoli florets.
Cut the chicken breast tenderloins into bite-size pieces. (You can totally use chicken thighs or whole breasts for this recipe.
I just saw these tenderloins at the grocery store and the price was right!).
Transfer the chicken to a medium mixing bowl with 1 tsp salt, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, and smoked paprika.
Toss until evenly coated.
Melt butter and olive oil in a large broiler pan or an oven-safe sauté pan over medium heat.
Add seasoned chicken.
Cook until the chicken is cooked through, about 6 minutes per side, 12-15 minutes total.
Next, add the orzo to the pan and toss it with the chicken to lightly toast it, about 2 minutes.
Deglaze the pan with the chicken broth.
Stir everything together and turn the heat down to medium-low.
Shred cheddar cheese and set aside.
Set oven to broil on high.
Add room temperature whole milk to the skillet and stir to combine.
Add chopped broccoli florets.
Simmer everything for about 8 minutes or until the orzo is done to your liking, and most of the liquid has been absorbed.
Stir in half of the cheddar cheese.
Add the rest of the cheddar cheese on top and sprinkle with the remaining salt and any extra pepper you might like.
Transfer to oven and broil for 3-5 minutes until the cheese has melted, or just put the lid on your pan and melt the cheese on the stovetop.

items.title: Garlic Herb Roasted Cherry Tomato Carbonara
items.creator: Half Baked Harvest
ingredients: 8 ounces burrata cheese, at room temperature
Calabrian chili flakes or jarred chilies in oil
steps: Preheat the oven to 425°F.
In a baking dish, toss the tomatoes with the olive oil, 2 tablespoons of herbs, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Arrange the prosciutto around the tomatoes.
Roast for 10–15 minutes, until the tomatoes burst and the prosciutto is crisp.2.
Meanwhile, whisk the egg yolks, whole egg, and Parmesan together in a large serving bowl.
Add the butter.3.
Cook the pasta until al dente.
Just before draining, reserve 1 cup of the pasta cooking water, then drain.4.
Immediately add the hot pasta to the egg mixture, tossing quickly to combine.
Add the hot pasta water a little at a time, tossing continuously, until the sauce is creamy and glossy.
Add the roasted tomatoes and all their juices.
Crumble in the crispy prosciutto and gently toss.
Season with freshly cracked black pepper.5.
Divide the pasta among plates.
Top with torn burrata, basil, and Calabrian chilies.
Serve immediately and start twirling!

items.title: Bread omelette
steps: Make and enjoy

items.title: Balchi di Pisca
steps: These delectable fish balls can also be made with salmon or fish fillets. Substitute one large can of salmon or one pound of any white fish for the cod.
Soak for twenty-four hours:
1 salted cod, or bakijow Discard the water.
Place cod in saucepan with fresh water to cover.
Simmer gently until the fish flakes easily when tested with the tines of a fork.
Strain, reserving a bit of the broth.
De bone the cod and set it aside for later use.
In a saucepan, bring to boil in water to cover: 3 medium potatoes, peeled and diced When the potatoes are tender, drain them well.
Add the cod and mash the two ingredients thoroughly together.
Place in the container of an electric blender:
1 tomato, peeled and chopped
1/2 green pepper, chopped
1 medium onion, peeled and chopped
1 clove garlic, slivered
1/2 tsp. Tabasco sauce, or minced hot pepper
Dash of nutmeg
Salt and pepper to taste
Blend for a few seconds and pour the sauce over the mashed fish mixture.

Combine these ingredients well and add 1 egg, beaten Mixture should be stiff enough to mold into balls about one and a half inches in diameter, If it's too dry, add the fish stock a tablespoon at a time.
Fry the balls in hot, deep fat until golden brown.

items.title: Tirolean Dumplings
steps: Finely chop the shallots, and dice the smoked ham or sausage into small cubes.
Heat some butter or clarified butter in a pan and sweat the onions in it until translucent.
Add the meat and the parsley and fry together briefly before removing from the heat.
Place the bread in a bowl.
Beat the milk with the eggs and season well with salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Pour over the bread.
Stir in the sausage and onion paste and mix in the flour.
Mix together to form a relatively firm paste (adding more bread or flour if necessary) and season again according to taste.
Smooth the surface of the dough out and leave to stand for approx.
30 minutes.
Heat up a good quantity of salted water in a large pan.
Use the paste to form smaller dumplings (for use as a garnish in soups) or medium-sized dumplings, as required.
Moisten the hands regularly with cold water during this stage so that the dumplings take on smooth forms.
Place in boiling water, bring back to the boil, turn down the heat, and simmer gently for 8-20 minutes, depending on the size.
Remove from the water, dry off well and serve up garnished with chopped parsley and melted butter (which has been taken on a nut-brown colour).

items.title: Jamaican Boiled Dumplings
steps: In a large pot, bring water and salt to a boil to boil the dumplings.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the all-purpose flour and salt, stirring to distribute the salt evenly throughout the flour.
Gradually add water to the flour mixture, mixing with your hands until a dough forms.
Divide the dough into equal-sized pieces, rolling each into a smooth ball. Flatten each ball slightly with the palm of your hand to form a round, circular dumpling. It should look like a thick disk.
Carefully drop the dumplings into the boiling water, one at a time, ensuring that they don't stick together. You can use a wooden spoon to stir the dumplings in the water.
Boil the dumplings for 15-20 minutes, or until they are cooked through and have risen to the surface of the water. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
Use a slotted spoon to remove the cooked dumplings from the pot, allowing any excess water to drain.
Serve with your favorite recipes.

items.title: Classic Christmas pudding
steps: Get everything for the pudding prepared.
Chop the almonds coarsely.
Peel, core and chop the cooking apples.
Sharpen your knife and chop the candied peel.
(You can chop the almonds and apples in a food processor, but the peel must be done by hand.) Grate three quarters of the nutmeg (sounds a lot but it's correct).
Mix the almonds, apples, candied peel, nutmeg, raisins, flour, breadcrumbs, light muscovado sugar, eggs and 2 tbsp brandy or cognac in a large bowl.
Holding the butter in its wrapper, grate a quarter of it into the bowl, then stir everything together.
Repeat until all the butter is grated, then stir for 3-4 mins – the mixture is ready when it subsides slightly after each stir.
Ask the family to stir too, and get everyone to make a wish.
Generously butter two 1.2 litre bowls and put a circle of baking parchment in the bottom of each.
Pack in the pudding mixture.
Cover with a double layer of baking parchment, pleating it to allow for expansion, then tie with string (keep the paper in place with a rubber band while tying).
Trim off any excess paper.

Now stand each bowl on a large sheet of foil and bring the edges up over the top, then put another sheet of foil over the top and bring it down underneath to make a double package (this makes the puddings watertight).
Tie with more string, and make a handle for easy lifting in and out of the pan.
Watch our video to see how to tie up a pudding correctly.
Boil or oven steam the puddings for 8 hrs, topping up with water as necessary.
Remove from the pans and leave to cool overnight.
When cold, discard the messy wrappings and re-wrap in new baking parchment, foil and string.
Store in a cool, dry place until Christmas.
To make the brandy butter, cream the butter with the orange zest and icing sugar.
Gradually beat in the brandy or cognac and chopped stem ginger.
Put in a small bowl, fork the top attractively and put in the fridge to set.
The butter will keep for a week in the fridge, or it can be frozen for up to six weeks.
On Christmas Day, boil or oven steam for 1 hr. Unwrap and turn out. To flame, warm 3-4 tbsp brandy in a small pan, pour it over the pudding and set light to it.

items.title: Holiday Wine-Braised Short Ribs
items.creator: Joan Nathan
ingredients: 6 pounds bone-in short ribs (at least 1 ½ inches thick), cut into 2- to 4-inch pieces
Coarse kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
2 carrots, cut on the diagonal into 2-inch pieces
2 tablespoons chopped fresh cilantro or parsley, for serving
Sichuan chile oil (optional), homemade or store-bought, for serving
steps: Heat oven to 250 degrees.
Place short ribs on a plate and season with salt and pepper.
Warm olive oil in a 7-quart Dutch oven (or other large, heavy ovenproof pot with a lid) over medium heat.
Using tongs, sear meat for about 3 minutes per side to give it some color.
Return the pieces to the plate, reserving the oil and fat in the pot.
Add onion to the Dutch oven and stir occasionally until softened, 5 to 7 minutes.
Stir in cumin, curry powder, cinnamon, brown sugar and ketchup.
Add meat along with red wine, ginger ale, soy sauce, tomato, jalapeño (if using), rosemary, bay leaves, carrots, and lastly the celery.
Cover and transfer to the oven.
Cook for about 4 hours, until the meat is fork-tender and falls off the bones.
Remove and discard the celery, rosemary, bay leaves and jalapeño (if used).
Let cool in the Dutch oven, then chill in the refrigerator at least overnight and up to 2 days.
When ready to serve, heat the oven to 350 degrees.
Remove and discard the solidified fat on top of the meat and reheat the short ribs, covered, in the oven until warmed through, about 20 minutes.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Transfer to a serving platter, sprinkle with cilantro or parsley and serve with a small bowl of Sichuan chile oil if you’d like.

items.title: Furikake
items.creator: Mia Leimkuhler
ingredients: 3 sheets unseasoned nori (dried seaweed sheets for sushi)
⅔ cup roasted sesame seeds (see Tip)
Optional mix-ins (add to taste): shichimi togarashi, gochugaru, crushed potato or corn chips, dried onion flakes, fried garlic (see Tip)
steps: Crumble the nori sheets into a food processor.
(If your nori sheets aren’t crisp enough to easily crumble, carefully toast them first by waving them over a gas flame or placing them under a broiler for a few seconds.)
Add the sesame seeds, salt, sugar and bonito flakes, if using, and pulse until the mixture is well blended and the nori pieces are about the size of grains of rice.
Stir in any additional mix-ins.
Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place or the fridge for up to one month.

items.title: Pommes Purée (French Mashed Potatoes)
items.creator: Alexia Duchêne
ingredients: 2 lb. 4 oz. large Yukon gold potatoes (5–7)
1 cup (2 sticks) chilled unsalted butter, sliced
A food mill and a fine-mesh tamis
steps: Place 2 lb.
4 oz. large Yukon gold potatoes (5–7) in a large pot and pour in water to cover by about 2".
Season generously with kosher salt and bring to a boil.
Cook until potatoes are fork-tender, 20–25 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat 1 cup whole milk in a small saucepan over low heat and keep warm.
Drain potatoes.
Working quickly so they remain hot, peel potatoes with a paring knife and cut into pieces.
Pass potatoes through food mill into a medium bowl, then pass through tamis onto a sheet of parchment paper, pressing with a heatproof rubber spatula.
Transfer potato purée to a small pot or large saucepan and cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until dried out a little and steaming, about 3 minutes.
Gradually pour in warm milk, stirring constantly until smooth and spoonable (you might not need all of the milk).
Remove from heat and add 1 cup (2 sticks) chilled unsalted butter, sliced, a few pieces at a time, whisking after each addition until melted and combined before adding more.
Taste pommes purée and season with salt as needed.

items.title: Pommes Dauphine
items.creator: Alexia Duchêne
ingredients: Coarse salt (kosher or sea; for baking potatoes)
1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt, plus more
Peanut oil (for frying and spoons; about 8 cups)
A food mill and a deep-fry thermometer
steps: Place a rack in middle of oven; preheat to 350°.
Sprinkle coarse salt over a rimmed baking sheet to cover (aim for a ¼"–½" thick layer).
Nestle 1 lb. large Yukon Gold potatoes (2–3) into the salt and roast in oven until a knife pierces through flesh with little resistance, about 30 minutes.
Remove from oven and, working quickly so potatoes remain hot, peel with a paring knife and halve.
Pass potatoes through food mill into a medium bowl; set aside.
Bring 4 Tbsp. unsalted butter, 1 tsp.
Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp.
Morton kosher salt, and ⅔ cup water to a simmer in a medium saucepan over high heat, stirring with a stiff heatproof spatula or sturdy rubber spatula to help melt butter and dissolve salt.
Immediately reduce heat to medium; add ⅔ cup all-purpose flour all at once and stir quickly until most of the flour is absorbed.
Cook, stirring vigorously and breaking up pockets of flour as needed, until a thin film forms on bottom and sides of pan and dough comes together into a single mass, 2–3 minutes.
(It should look glossy and feel buttery and smooth.) Remove from heat and let sit in pan until no longer hot but still warm, about 3 minutes.
Add 2 large eggs to mixture one at a time, mixing until incorporated after each addition.
Pâte à choux should be thick, glossy, and fall off spatula in a V-shape.
If it’s too thick, stir in another 1 large egg.
Add dough to reserved potatoes and stir to combine; season with kosher salt.
Pour peanut oil into a medium Dutch oven or large heavy saucepan fitted with thermometer to come 3" up sides (about 8 cups).
Heat over medium-high until thermometer registers 360°.
Reduce heat to medium (you want to maintain the temperature).
Using a spoon lightly coated in oil and working in batches of 6–8, spoon irregular amounts of batter into pot.
Fry, turning often, until golden brown all over, about 4 minutes.
Using a spider or slotted spoon, transfer to a rimmed baking sheet lined with paper towels to drain and immediately season with kosher salt.
Repeat process with remaining batter, adjusting heat as needed to maintain temperature.
Transfer pommes dauphine to a platter to serve.

items.title: Pommes Anna
items.creator: Alexia Duchêne
ingredients: 5 lb. large Yukon Gold potatoes (10–15), peeled
½ cup (1 stick) unsalted butter, sliced
steps: Place a rack in middle of oven; preheat to 400°.
Slice 5 lb. large Yukon gold potatoes (10–15), peeled, lengthwise on a mandoline set to 1-mm thickness.
Brush a large high-sided skillet with some of 1¼ cups clarified butter to coat.
Cut a round of parchment paper to fit bottom of pan and place in pan.
Brush parchment with more clarified butter.
Using cutter and working with a few slices stacked together at a time, punch out enough rounds to fill bottom of pan.
Arrange slices around sides of pan, overlapping slightly, to create a circle (make sure slices are compact and tight).
Repeat process, creating concentric circles, until you have an even layer covering entire bottom of pan.
Drizzle with some clarified butter and generously season with kosher salt.
Repeat process (no need to cut potatoes into rounds), creating more layers, until all of the potatoes slices and clarified butter have been used.
Dot ½ cup (1 stick) unsalted butter, sliced, over final layer of potatoes.
Cover pan with a lid or foil and bake potatoes until tender, 50–55 minutes.
Uncover and bake until deep golden brown in spots, 45–55 minutes more.
Let cool slightly, then place a plate upside down over pan.
Holding plate and pan together, carefully turn over in one swift motion to invert pommes Anna onto plate.
Remove pan.
